title.zh: 卷9 志第4 禮儀四
title.raw: 卷9 志第4 禮儀四 Volume 9 Treatises 4: Rites 4

sentences.zh: 禮儀四

translations.literal: Rites, Part Four.
translations.idiomatic: Rites, Part Four

sentences.zh: 周大定元年，靜帝遣兼太傅、上柱國、杞國公椿，大宗伯、大將軍、金城公煚，奉皇帝璽紱策書，禪位於隋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dadading of Zhou, Emperor Jing dispatched the concurrent Grand Tutor, Pillar of State, Duke Chun of Qi, and the Grand Herald, Grand General, Duke Jiong of Jincheng, bearing the imperial seal-cord and investiture scroll, to abdicate the throne to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Dadading 1, Emperor Jing sent the concurrent Grand Tutor and Pillar of State, Duke Chun of Qi, together with the Grand Herald and Grand General, Duke Jiong of Jincheng, bearing the imperial seal, cord, and investiture scroll to abdicate in favor of Sui.

sentences.zh: 司錄虞慶則白，請設壇於東第。

translations.literal: Director of Records Yu Qingze reported, requesting that an altar be set up at the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Records Yu Qingze submitted a memorial requesting that an altar be erected at the Eastern Residence.

sentences.zh: 博士何妥議，以為受禪登壇，以告天也，故魏受漢禪，設壇於繁昌，為在行旅，郊壇乃闕。

translations.literal: Erudite He Tuo argued that ascending the altar to receive the abdication was to report to Heaven; thus when Wei received the Han abdication, an altar was set up at Fanchang — being on campaign, the suburban altar was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite He Tuo argued that mounting the altar to receive the abdication was an announcement to Heaven. When Wei accepted the Han abdication, an altar was erected at Fanchang; because the court was on campaign, the suburban altar was omitted.

sentences.zh: 至如漢高在汜，光武在鄗，盡非京邑所築壇。

translations.literal: As for Gaozu of Han at Si and Guangwu at Hao, none of these altars were built in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han was at Si and Guangwu at Hao, neither built the altar in the capital city.

sentences.zh: 自晉、宋揖讓，皆在都下，莫不並就南郊，更無別築之義。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward, all abdications took place in the capital, invariably at the Southern Suburb, with no rationale for building a separate altar.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin and Song onward, every peaceful transfer of power took place in the capital, always at the Southern Suburb, with no precedent for erecting a separate altar.

sentences.zh: 又後魏即位，登硃雀觀，周帝初立，受朝于路門，雖自我作古，皆非禮也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Later Wei acceded, they mounted the Vermilion Sparrow Tower; when the Zhou emperor was first installed, he received court at the Road Gate — though innovations of their own making, none accorded with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei had the new emperor ascend the Vermilion Sparrow Tower; when the Zhou emperor was first enthroned, he received court at the Road Gate. Though each dynasty invented its own practice, none was proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 今即府為壇，恐招後誚。

translations.literal: Now to make the residence itself the altar would, I fear, invite later reproach.
translations.idiomatic: To use the residence itself as the altar would, I fear, invite reproach from later ages.

sentences.zh: 議者從之。

translations.literal: The debaters agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 二月甲子，椿等乘象輅，備鹵簿，持節，率百官至門下，奉策入次。

translations.literal: On jiazi of the second month, Chun and the others rode the elephant carriage, with full guard of honor, bearing the staff of authority, leading the hundred officials to the gate, and deposited the investiture scroll in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the second month, Chun and his party rode the elephant carriage with full guard of honor and staff of authority, led the hundred officials to the gate, and placed the investiture scroll in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 百官文武，朝服立于門南，北面。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials, in court dress, stood south of the gate, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials in court dress stood south of the gate, facing north.

sentences.zh: 高祖冠遠遊冠，府僚陪列。

translations.literal: Gaozu wore the far-wandering cap; the staff of the residence lined up beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wore the far-wandering cap, with the staff of the residence arrayed in attendance.

sentences.zh: 記室入白，禮曹導高祖，府僚從，出大門東廂西向。

translations.literal: The recorder entered to announce; the ritual officer guided Gaozu, the staff following, out through the great gate to the eastern wing, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The recorder entered to announce; the ritual officer led Gaozu out through the great gate to the eastern wing, facing west, with the staff following.

sentences.zh: 椿奉策書，煚奉璽紱，出次，節導而進。

translations.literal: Chun bore the investiture scroll, Jiong bore the seal and cord; they came out from the side chamber and advanced under guidance of the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Chun carried the investiture scroll and Jiong the seal and cord; they emerged from the side chamber and advanced under the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 高祖揖之，入門而左，椿等入門而右。

translations.literal: Gaozu bowed to them; entering the gate he turned left, while Chun and the others entered and turned right.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu bowed to them, entered the gate and turned left; Chun and the others entered and turned right.

sentences.zh: 百官隨入庭中。

translations.literal: The hundred officials followed into the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials followed them into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 椿南向，讀冊書畢，進授高祖。

translations.literal: Chun, facing south, finished reading the bound scroll and stepped forward to present it to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Facing south, Chun finished reading the bound scroll and stepped forward to present it to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖北面再拜，辭不奉詔。

translations.literal: Gaozu, facing north, bowed twice and declined to accept the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu faced north, bowed twice, and declined the mandate.

sentences.zh: 上柱國李穆進喻朝旨，又與百官勸進，高祖不納。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Li Mu stepped forward to explain the court's intent, and together with the hundred officials urged him to accept; Gaozu would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Li Mu stepped forward to explain the court's intent and, with the hundred officials, pressed him to accept; Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 椿等又奉策書進而敦勸，高祖再拜，俯受策，以授高熲；

translations.literal: Chun and the others again presented the investiture scroll and pressed him earnestly; Gaozu bowed twice, bowed his head to receive the scroll, and handed it to Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and the others again presented the investiture scroll and pressed him earnestly. Gaozu bowed twice, bowed his head to receive the scroll, and handed it to Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 受璽，以授虞慶則。

translations.literal: He received the seal and handed it to Yu Qingze.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the seal, he handed it to Yu Qingze.

sentences.zh: 退就東階位。

translations.literal: He withdrew to take his place on the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and took his place on the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 使者與百官皆北面再拜，搢笏，三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The envoys and the hundred officials all faced north, bowed twice, inserted their tablets, and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: The envoys and the hundred officials all faced north, bowed twice, tucked their tablets, and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 有司請備法駕，高祖不許，改服紗帽、黃袍，入幸臨光殿。

translations.literal: The relevant office requested preparation of the imperial carriage; Gaozu did not permit it, changed into gauze cap and yellow robe, and entered to attend at the Lincang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office requested the imperial carriage; Gaozu refused, changed into a gauze cap and yellow robe, and entered the Lincang Hall.

sentences.zh: 就閣內服袞冕，乘小輿，出自西序，如元會儀。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion he donned the dragon robe and crown, rode the small palanquin, came out from the western gallery, and proceeded according to the New Year's audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: Within the pavilion he donned the dragon robe and crown, rode the small palanquin out from the western gallery, and proceeded according to the New Year's audience rite.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書以案承符命及祥瑞牒，進東階下。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites, bearing a tray with the mandate tokens and auspicious memorials, advanced below the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites, bearing a tray with the mandate tokens and memorials of auspicious omens, advanced below the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 納言跪御前以聞。

translations.literal: The Chief Counselor knelt before the throne to report.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Counselor knelt before the throne to report.

sentences.zh: 內史令奉宣詔大赦，改元曰開皇。

translations.literal: The Palace Secretary proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Secretary then proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 是日，命有司奉冊祀於南郊。

translations.literal: That day, he ordered the relevant office to offer the bound scroll in sacrifice at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ordered the relevant office to offer the bound scroll in sacrifice at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 後齊將崇皇太后，則太尉以玉帛告圓丘方澤，以幣告廟。

translations.literal: When Later Qi was about to honor the Empress Dowager, the Grand Commandant reported with jade and silk at the Round Mound and Square Pond, and with silks at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before Later Qi could honor the Empress Dowager, the Grand Commandant reported with jade and silk at the Round Mound and Square Pond, and with silks at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乃臨軒，命太保持節，太尉副之。

translations.literal: The emperor then came to the front hall and ordered the Grand Mentor to bear the staff of authority, with the Grand Commandant as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then came to the front hall and ordered the Grand Mentor to bear the staff of authority, with the Grand Commandant as deputy.

sentences.zh: 設九儐，命使者受璽綬冊及節，詣西上閤。

translations.literal: Nine ushers were appointed; the envoys received the seal, cord, bound scroll, and staff of authority, and proceeded to the Western Upper Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Nine ushers were appointed; the envoys received the seal, cord, bound scroll, and staff of authority and proceeded to the Western Upper Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其日，昭陽殿文物具陳，臨軒訖，使者就位，持節及璽綬稱詔。

translations.literal: On that day the regalia was fully displayed in Zhaoyang Hall; when the emperor had come to the front hall and the envoys were in place, they bore the staff of authority and seal-cord and proclaimed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: That day the regalia was fully displayed in Zhaoyang Hall. When the emperor had come to the front hall and the envoys were in place, they bore the staff of authority and seal-cord and proclaimed the edict.

sentences.zh: 二侍中拜進，受節及冊璽綬，以付小黃門。

translations.literal: The two attendants-in-ordinary bowed and advanced, received the staff of authority and bound scroll with seal-cord, and handed them to the junior yellow gate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Both attendants-in-ordinary bowed and advanced, received the staff of authority and bound scroll with seal-cord, and handed them to the junior yellow gate attendants.

sentences.zh: 黃門以詣閤。

translations.literal: The yellow gate attendants proceeded to the pavilion with them.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow gate attendants carried them to the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皇太后服褘衣，處昭陽殿，公主及命婦陪列於殿，皆拜。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wore the hui robe, seated herself in Zhaoyang Hall; princesses and titled ladies lined the hall and all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wore the hui robe and seated herself in Zhaoyang Hall; princesses and titled ladies lined the hall and all bowed.

sentences.zh: 小黃門以節綬入，女侍中受，以進皇太后。

translations.literal: The junior yellow gate attendants entered with the staff and cord; the female attendant-in-ordinary received them and presented them to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Junior yellow gate attendants entered with the staff and cord; the female attendant-in-ordinary received them and presented them to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 皇太后興，受，以授左右。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager rose, received them, and handed them to attendants at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Rising, the Empress Dowager, received them, and handed them to attendants at her side.

sentences.zh: 複坐，反節于使者。

translations.literal: She seated herself again and returned the staff of authority to the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Seating herself again, she returned the staff of authority to the envoys.

sentences.zh: 使者受節出。

translations.literal: The envoys received the staff of authority and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys took the staff of authority and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冊皇后，如太后之禮。

translations.literal: Investiture of the empress followed the rites for the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Investiture of the empress followed the same rites as for the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 後齊冊皇太子，則皇帝臨軒，司待為使，司空副之。

translations.literal: When Later Qi invested the crown prince, the emperor came to the front hall; the Director of Attendants served as envoy, with the Minister of Works as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: For Later Qi's investiture of the crown prince, the emperor came to the front hall; the Director of Attendants served as envoy, with the Minister of Works as deputy.

sentences.zh: 太子服遠遊冠，入至位。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the far-wandering cap and entered to his place.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing the far-wandering cap, the crown prince the far-wandering cap and entered to his place.

sentences.zh: 使者入，奉冊讀訖，皇太子跪受冊於使，以授中庶子。

translations.literal: The envoy entered, presented the bound scroll and finished reading; the crown prince knelt to receive the scroll from the envoy and handed it to the junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Entering, the envoy presented the bound scroll and finished reading; the crown prince knelt to receive the scroll from the envoy and handed it to the junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 又受璽綬于尚書，以授庶子。

translations.literal: He also received the seal and cord from the Minister of Works and handed them to the tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise received the seal and cord from the Minister of Works and handed them to the tutor.

sentences.zh: 稽首以出。

translations.literal: He bowed his forehead to the ground and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 就冊，則使者持節至東宮，宮臣內外官定列。

translations.literal: For investiture at the residence, the envoy bore the staff of authority to the Eastern Palace; inner and outer palace officials took their fixed places.
translations.idiomatic: When investiture took place at the residence, the envoy bore the staff of authority to the Eastern Palace; inner and outer palace officials took their fixed places.

sentences.zh: 皇太子階東，西面。

translations.literal: The crown prince stood east of the steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Standing east of the steps, the crown prince east of the steps, facing west.

sentences.zh: 若幼，則太師抱之，主衣二人奉空頂幘服從，以受冊。

translations.literal: If he was young, the Grand Tutor held him; two masters of robes bore the empty-topped cap and robe to follow, to receive the investiture scroll.
translations.idiomatic: If he was still a child, the Grand Tutor held him while two masters of robes followed bearing the empty-topped cap and robe for him to receive the investiture scroll.

sentences.zh: 明日，拜章表於東宮殿庭，中庶子、中舍人乘軺車，奉章詣朝堂謝。

translations.literal: The next day he presented a memorial of thanks in the courtyard of the Eastern Palace; the junior tutor and junior attendant rode the light carriage, bearing the memorial to the court hall to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day he presented a memorial of thanks in the courtyard of the Eastern Palace; the junior tutor and junior attendant rode the light carriage, bearing the memorial to the court hall to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 擇日齋於崇正殿，服冕，乘石山安車謁廟。

translations.literal: On a chosen day he fasted at the Chongzheng Hall, donned the crown robe, and rode the stone-mount carriage to visit the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day he fasted at the Chongzheng Hall, donned the crown robe, and rode the stone-mount carriage to visit the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 擇日群臣上禮，又擇日會。

translations.literal: On a chosen day the ministers presented congratulatory gifts; on another chosen day there was a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On a selected day the ministers presented congratulatory gifts; on another chosen day there was a banquet.

sentences.zh: 明日，三品以上箋賀。

translations.literal: The next day, officials of third rank and above submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, officials of third rank and above submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 冊諸王，以臨軒日上水一刻，吏部令史乘馬，齎召版，詣王第。

translations.literal: To invest princes, on the day of the front-hall audience, at one quarter after the fifth watch the clerks of the Ministry of Personnel rode forth bearing the summons tablet to the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: To invest princes, on the day of the front-hall audience, one quarter after the fifth watch the clerks of the Ministry of Personnel rode forth bearing the summons tablet to the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 王乘高車，鹵簿至東掖門止，乘軺車。

translations.literal: The prince rode the high carriage; the guard of honor halted at the Eastern Side Gate, and he transferred to the light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the high carriage, the prince the high carriage; the guard of honor halted at the Eastern Side Gate, and he transferred to the light carriage.

sentences.zh: 既入，至席。

translations.literal: Having entered, he came to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, he came to his seat.

sentences.zh: 尚書讀冊訖，以授王，又授章綬。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works finished reading the bound scroll and presented it to the prince, then presented the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: After the Minister of Works finished reading the bound scroll and presented it to the prince, then presented the seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 事畢，乘軺車，入鹵簿，乘高車，詣閶闔門，伏闕表謝。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he rode the light carriage, rejoined the guard of honor, rode the high carriage to the Changhe Gate, and prostrated himself before the gate to submit a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: With the rite complete, he rode the light carriage, rejoined the guard of honor, rode the high carriage to the Changhe Gate, and prostrated himself before the gate to submit a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 報訖，拜廟還第。

translations.literal: When the reply was received, he visited the temple and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Once the reply was received, he visited the temple and returned to his residence.

sentences.zh: 就第，則鴻臚卿持節，吏部尚書授冊，侍御史授節。

translations.literal: At the residence, the Director of Banquets bore the staff of authority; the Minister of Personnel presented the bound scroll; the attendant censor presented the staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the prince's residence, the Director of Banquets bore the staff of authority; the Minister of Personnel presented the bound scroll; the attendant censor presented the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 使者受而出，乘軺車，持節，詣王第。

translations.literal: The envoy received them and withdrew, rode the light carriage, bore the staff of authority, and proceeded to the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy received them and withdrew, rode the light carriage, bore the staff of authority, and proceeded to the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 入就西階，東面。

translations.literal: He entered and took his place on the western steps, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Entering, he took his place on the western steps, facing east.

sentences.zh: 王入，立於東階，西面。

translations.literal: The prince entered and stood on the eastern steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The prince entered and took his stand on the eastern steps, facing west.

sentences.zh: 使者讀冊，博士讀版，王俯伏。

translations.literal: The envoy read the bound scroll; the erudite read the tablet; the prince bowed prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy then read the bound scroll; the erudite read the tablet; the prince bowed prostrate.

sentences.zh: 興，進受冊章綬茅土，俯伏三稽首，還本位，謝如上儀。

translations.literal: He rose, stepped forward to receive the bound scroll, seal, cord, and fief soil, bowed prostrate three times with forehead to the ground, returned to his place, and gave thanks according to the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: He rose, stepped forward to receive the bound scroll, seal, cord, and fief soil, kowtowed three times, returned to his place, and gave thanks according to the rite above.

sentences.zh: 在州鎮，則使者受節冊，乘軺車至州，如王第。

translations.literal: At a provincial post, the envoy received the staff of authority and bound scroll, rode the light carriage to the province, and proceeded as at the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: At a provincial post, the envoy received the staff of authority and bound scroll, rode the light carriage to the province, and proceeded as at the prince's residence, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 諸王、三公、儀同、尚書令、五等開國、太妃、妃、公主恭拜冊，軸一枚，長二尺，以白練衣之。

translations.literal: For princes, the Three Dukes, Commissioners with Equal Status, Ministers of Works, fifth-rank founding marquises, grand consorts, consorts, and princesses, the investiture scroll had one roller, two feet long, wrapped in white silk.
translations.idiomatic: For princes, the Three Dukes, commissioners with equal status, ministers of works, fifth-rank founding marquises, grand consorts, consorts, and princesses, the investiture scroll had one roller two feet long, wrapped in white silk.

sentences.zh: 用竹簡十二枚，六枚與軸等，六枚長尺二寸。

translations.literal: Twelve bamboo slips were used; six matched the roller in length, six were one foot two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bamboo slips were used: six matched the roller in length, six were one foot two inches long.

sentences.zh: 文出集書，書皆篆字。

translations.literal: The text came from the Secretariat; all writing was in seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All text came from the Secretariat; all writing was in seal script.

sentences.zh: 哀冊、贈冊亦同。

translations.literal: Lament scrolls and posthumous investiture scrolls were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Lament scrolls and posthumous investiture scrolls followed the same format.

sentences.zh: 諸王、五等開國及鄉男恭拜，以其封國所在方，取社壇方面土，包以白茅，內青箱中。

translations.literal: For princes, fifth-rank founding marquises, and district barons, in the direction of their fief they took earth from the corresponding side of the altar of the soil, wrapped it in white thatch, and placed it in a blue chest.
translations.idiomatic: For princes, fifth-rank founding marquises, and district barons, earth was taken from the corresponding side of the altar of the soil in the direction of their fief, wrapped in white thatch, and placed in a blue chest.

sentences.zh: 函方五寸，以青塗飾，封授之，以為社。

translations.literal: The case was five inches square, decorated with blue lacquer, sealed and presented — this served as the altar of the soil.
translations.idiomatic: The case was five inches square, decorated with blue lacquer, sealed and presented — this represented the altar of the soil.

sentences.zh: 隋臨軒冊命三師、諸王、三公，並陳車輅。

translations.literal: Under Sui, at the front-hall audience to invest the Three Preceptors, princes, and Three Dukes, chariots and carriages were all displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, when investing the Three Preceptors, princes, and Three Dukes at the front-hall audience, chariots and carriages were all displayed.

sentences.zh: 餘則否。

translations.literal: For the others, this was not done.
translations.idiomatic: For other investitures, this was not done.

sentences.zh: 百司定列，內史令讀冊訖，受冊者拜受出。

translations.literal: The hundred offices took their fixed places; the Palace Secretary finished reading the bound scroll; the recipient bowed, received it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: All hundred offices took their fixed places; the Palace Secretary finished reading the bound scroll; the recipient bowed, received it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又引次受冊者，如上儀。

translations.literal: The next recipient was then led in, according to the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: The next recipient was then led in according to the rite above.

sentences.zh: 若冊開國，郊社令奉茅土，立于仗南，西面。

translations.literal: When investing a founding marquis, the Director of Suburban Sacrifices presented the fief soil and stood south of the guard of honor, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In investing a founding marquis, the Director of Suburban Sacrifices presented the fief soil and stood south of the guard of honor, facing west.

sentences.zh: 每受冊訖，授茅土焉。

translations.literal: After each investiture was complete, the fief soil was presented.
translations.idiomatic: Upon each investiture was complete, the fief soil was presented.

sentences.zh: 後齊皇帝加元服，以玉帛告圓丘方澤，以幣告廟，擇日臨軒。

translations.literal: When the Later Qi emperor performed the capping rite, jade and silk were reported at the Round Mound and Square Pond, silks at the temple; on a chosen day he came to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Qi emperor performed the capping rite, jade and silk were reported at the Round Mound and Square Pond and silks at the temple; on a chosen day he came to the front hall.

sentences.zh: 中嚴，群官位定，皇帝著空頂介幘以出。

translations.literal: At the second watch the officials took their places; the emperor came out wearing the empty-topped cap with black headband.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch, officials took their places; the emperor came out wearing the empty-topped cap with black headband.

sentences.zh: 太尉盥訖，升，脫空頂幘，以黑介幘奉加訖，太尉進太保之右，北面讀祝訖，太保加冕，侍中系玄紱，脫絳紗袍，加袞服，事畢，太保上壽，群官三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: When the Grand Commandant had finished washing, he ascended, removed the empty-topped cap, placed the black headband cap, finished reading the invocation, the Grand Mentor placed the crown, the attendant-in-ordinary tied the black cord, removed the crimson gauze robe and added the dragon robe; when complete, the Grand Mentor offered the longevity toast, and the officials thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Commandant had finished washing, he ascended, removed the empty-topped cap, placed the black headband cap, and finished reading the invocation. The Grand Mentor placed the crown; the attendant-in-ordinary tied the black cord, removed the crimson gauze robe, and added the dragon robe. When complete, the Grand Mentor offered the longevity toast and the officials thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 皇帝入溫室，移禦坐，會而不上壽。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the warming chamber, moved the imperial seat, and held a banquet without the longevity toast.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the warming chamber, moved the imperial seat, and held a banquet without the longevity toast.

sentences.zh: 後日，文武群官朝服，上禮酒十二鐘，米十二囊，牛十二頭。

translations.literal: On a later day the civil and military officials in court dress presented twelve jars of ceremonial wine, twelve sacks of rice, and twelve oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, civil and military officials in court dress presented twelve jars of ceremonial wine, twelve sacks of rice, and twelve oxen.

sentences.zh: 又擇日親拜圓丘方澤，謁廟。

translations.literal: On another chosen day he personally worshipped at the Round Mound and Square Pond and visited the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day he personally worshipped at the Round Mound and Square Pond and visited the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冠，則太尉以制幣告七廟，擇日臨軒。

translations.literal: For the crown prince's capping, the Grand Commandant reported to the seven temples with prescribed silks; on a chosen day the emperor came to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: For the crown prince's capping, the Grand Commandant reported to the seven temples with prescribed silks; on a chosen day the emperor came to the front hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 有司供帳於崇正殿。

translations.literal: The relevant office supplied the pavilion at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office prepared the pavilion at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 中嚴，皇太子空頂幘公服出，立東階之南，西面，使者入，立西階之南，東面。

translations.literal: At the second watch the crown prince came out in empty-topped cap and official dress, standing south of the eastern steps facing west; the envoy entered and stood south of the western steps facing east.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch, the crown prince came out in empty-topped cap and official dress, standing south of the eastern steps facing west; the envoy entered and stood south of the western steps facing east.

sentences.zh: 皇太子受詔訖，入室盥櫛，出，南面。

translations.literal: When the crown prince had received the edict, he entered the chamber to wash and comb, came out, and faced south.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the edict, the crown prince entered the chamber to wash and comb, came out, and faced south.

sentences.zh: 使者進揖，詣冠席，西面坐。

translations.literal: The envoy stepped forward with a bow, proceeded to the capping seat, and sat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy bowed and stepped forward with a bow, proceeded to the capping seat, and sat facing west.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿盥訖，詣太子前疏櫛。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonial Affairs finished washing and came before the crown prince to comb his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Having washed, the Director of Ceremonial Affairs and came before the crown prince to comb his hair.

sentences.zh: 使者又盥，奉進賢三梁冠，至太子前，東面祝，脫空頂幘，加冠。

translations.literal: The envoy washed again, presented the three-ridge cap of advancing worthies, came before the crown prince, faced east to invoke, removed the empty-topped cap, and placed the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Washing again, the envoy presented the three-ridge cap of advancing worthies, came before the crown prince, faced east to invoke, removed the empty-topped cap, and placed the crown.

sentences.zh: 太子興，入室更衣，出，又南面就席。

translations.literal: The crown prince rose, entered the chamber to change clothes, came out, and again faced south to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Rising, the crown prince entered the chamber to change clothes, came out, and again faced south to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿盥櫛。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonial Affairs washed and combed.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonial Affairs washed and combed again.

sentences.zh: 使者又盥祝，脫三梁冠，加遠遊冠。

translations.literal: The envoy washed again and invoked, removed the three-ridge cap, and placed the far-wandering cap.
translations.idiomatic: After washing again and invoking, removed the three-ridge cap, and placed the far-wandering cap.

sentences.zh: 太子又入室更衣。

translations.literal: The crown prince again entered the chamber to change clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Once more the crown prince entered the chamber to change clothes.

sentences.zh: 設席中楹之西，使者揖就席，南面。

translations.literal: A mat was set west of the central pillar; the envoy bowed and took his seat facing south.
translations.idiomatic: They set a mat west of the central pillar; the envoy bowed and took his seat facing south.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿洗爵酌醴，使者詣席前，北面祝。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonial Affairs washed the cup and poured the ceremonial wine; the envoy came before the mat and faced north to invoke.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonial Affairs washed the cup and and poured the ceremonial wine; the envoy came before the mat and faced north to invoke.

sentences.zh: 太子拜受醴，即席坐，祭之，啐之，奠爵，降階，複本位，西面。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed to receive the wine, sat on the mat, offered a libation, sipped it, placed the cup, descended the steps, returned to his place, and faced west.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing, the crown prince received the wine, sat on the mat, offered a libation, sipped it, placed the cup, descended the steps, returned to his place, and faced west.

sentences.zh: 三師、三少及在位群官拜事訖。

translations.literal: The Three Preceptors, Three Junior Preceptors, and assembled officials bowed; the rite was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Three Preceptors, Three Junior Preceptors, and assembled officials bowed; the rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 又擇日會宮臣，又擇日謁廟。

translations.literal: On another chosen day he convened the palace officials; on another chosen day he visited the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day he convened the palace officials; on another chosen day he visited the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 隋皇太子將冠，前一日，皇帝齋于大興殿。

translations.literal: When the Sui crown prince was about to be capped, on the day before the emperor fasted in the Daxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui crown prince was to be capped, the day before the emperor fasted in the Daxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太子與賓贊及預從官齋於正寢。

translations.literal: The crown prince, the guest and assistant, and attendant officials all fasted in the principal chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, the guest and assistant of the rite, and attendant officials all fasted in the principal chamber.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，有司告廟，各設筵於阼階。

translations.literal: At daybreak on the day, the relevant office reported to the temple; each set a mat on the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the relevant office reported to the temple, and a mat was set on the eastern steps for each.

sentences.zh: 皇帝袞冕入拜，即御座。

translations.literal: The emperor in dragon robe and crown entered to bow, then took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in dragon robe and crown, entered to bow and then took the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 賓揖皇太子進，升筵，西向坐。

translations.literal: The guest bowed and led the crown prince forward; he ascended the mat and sat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing, the guest and led the crown prince forward; he ascended the mat and sat facing west.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者坐櫛，設纚。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap sat to comb and set the hairnet.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant of the cap sat to comb his hair and set the hairnet.

sentences.zh: 賓盥訖，進加緇布冠。

translations.literal: When the guest had finished washing, he stepped forward and placed the black cloth cap.
translations.idiomatic: After washing, the guest stepped forward and placed the black cloth cap.

sentences.zh: 贊冠進設頍纓。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap stepped forward to set the forehead band and tassel.
translations.idiomatic: The cap assistant stepped forward to set the forehead band and tassel.

sentences.zh: 賓揖皇太子適東序，衣玄衣素裳以出。

translations.literal: The guest bowed and led the crown prince to the eastern gallery; he came out in dark upper garment and plain lower skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The guest bowed and led the crown prince to the eastern gallery; he emerged in dark upper garment and plain lower skirt.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者又坐櫛，賓進加遠遊冠。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap again sat to comb; the guest stepped forward and placed the far-wandering cap.
translations.idiomatic: The cap assistant again sat to comb; the guest stepped forward and placed the far-wandering cap.

sentences.zh: 改服訖，賓又受冕。

translations.literal: When the change of dress was complete, the guest again received the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Once the change of dress was complete, the guest again received the crown.

sentences.zh: 太子適東序，改服以出。

translations.literal: The crown prince went to the eastern gallery, changed clothes, and came out.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince then went to the eastern gallery, changed clothes, and came out.

sentences.zh: 賓揖皇太子南面立，賓進受醴，進筵前，北面立祝。

translations.literal: The guest bowed and led the crown prince to stand facing south; the guest stepped forward to receive the ceremonial wine, came before the mat, and stood facing north to invoke.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing, the guest and led the crown prince to stand facing south; the guest stepped forward to receive the ceremonial wine, came before the mat, and stood facing north to invoke.

sentences.zh: 皇太子拜受觶。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed to receive the cup.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing, the crown prince to receive the cup.

sentences.zh: 賓復位，東面答拜。

translations.literal: The guest returned to his place and answered the bow facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The guest returned to his place and returned the bow facing east.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者奉饌於筵前，皇太子祭奠。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap presented the food before the mat; the crown prince offered the libation.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant of the cap presented the food before the mat, and the crown prince offered the libation.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，降筵，進當禦東面拜。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he descended from the mat, advanced, and bowed east of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: With the rite complete, he descended from the mat, advanced, and bowed east of the throne.

sentences.zh: 納言承詔，詣太子戒訖，太子拜。

translations.literal: The Chief Counselor received the edict, proceeded to admonish the crown prince, and when finished the crown prince bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the edict, the Chief Counselor the edict, proceeded to admonish the crown prince, and when finished the crown prince bowed.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者引太子降自西階。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap led the crown prince down the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The cap assistant led the crown prince down the western steps.

sentences.zh: 賓少進，字之。

translations.literal: The guest stepped forward slightly and bestowed the style name.
translations.idiomatic: Stepping forward slightly, the guest and bestowed the style name.

sentences.zh: 贊冠者引皇太子進，立於庭，東面。

translations.literal: The assistant of the cap led the crown prince forward to stand in the courtyard facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The cap assistant led the crown prince forward to stand in the courtyard facing east.

sentences.zh: 諸親拜訖，贊冠者拜，太子皆答拜。

translations.literal: When the relatives had finished bowing, the assistant of the cap bowed; the crown prince returned each bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the relatives had finished bowing, the assistant of the cap bowed, and the crown prince returned each bow.

sentences.zh: 與賓贊俱復位。

translations.literal: He and the guest and assistant all returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: He, the guest and assistant all returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 納言承詔降，令有司致禮。

translations.literal: The Chief Counselor received the edict and descended, ordering the relevant office to present gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the edict, the Chief Counselor the edict and descended, ordering the relevant office to present gifts.

sentences.zh: 賓贊又拜。

translations.literal: The guest and assistant bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: The guest and assistant bowed again, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降複阼階，拜，皇太子已下皆拜。

translations.literal: The emperor descended and returned to the eastern steps and bowed; the crown prince and those below all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended to the eastern steps and bowed; the crown prince and those below all bowed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出，更衣還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor withdrew, changed clothes, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawing, the emperor, changed clothes, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太子從至闕，因入見皇后，拜而還。

translations.literal: The crown prince followed to the gate, then entered to see the empress, bowed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Following to the gate, the crown prince to the gate, then entered to see the empress, bowed, and returned.

sentences.zh: 後齊皇帝納後之禮，納采、問名、納征訖，告圓丘方澤及廟，如加元服，是日，皇帝臨軒，命太尉為使，司徒副之。

translations.literal: The Later Qi rite for the emperor taking an empress: after initial gift, name inquiry, and betrothal gifts were complete, the Round Mound, Square Pond, and temple were notified as at the capping rite; on that day the emperor came to the front hall and ordered the Grand Commandant as envoy, with the Minister of Education as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Qi rite for the emperor taking an empress, after the initial gift, name inquiry, and betrothal gifts were complete, the Round Mound, Square Pond, and temple were notified as at the capping rite. That day the emperor came to the front hall and ordered the Grand Commandant as envoy, with the Minister of Education as deputy.

sentences.zh: 持節詣皇后行宮，東向，奉璽綬冊，以授中常侍。

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of authority he proceeded to the empress's traveling palace, faced east, presented the seal, cord, and bound scroll, and handed them to the palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Staff in hand, he of authority he proceeded to the empress's traveling palace, faced east, presented the seal, cord, and bound scroll, and handed them to the palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊于行殿。

translations.literal: The empress received the bound scroll in the traveling hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the traveling hall, the empress received the bound scroll in the traveling hall.

sentences.zh: 使者出，與公卿以下皆拜。

translations.literal: The envoy withdrew; he and the dukes and officials below all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy withdrew, and he and the dukes and officials below all bowed.

sentences.zh: 有司備迎禮。

translations.literal: The relevant office prepared the welcoming rite.
translations.idiomatic: Officials prepared the welcoming rite.

sentences.zh: 太保太尉，受詔而行。

translations.literal: The Grand Mentor and Grand Commandant received the edict and set out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor and Grand Commandant and Grand Commandant received the edict and set out.

sentences.zh: 主人公服，迎拜於門。

translations.literal: The host in mourning dress welcomed and bowed at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning dress, the host dress welcomed and bowed at the gate.

sentences.zh: 使者入，升自賓階，東面。

translations.literal: The envoy entered and ascended by the guest steps, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Entering, the envoy and ascended by the guest steps, facing east.

sentences.zh: 主人升自阼階，西面。

translations.literal: The host ascended by the host steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host then ascended by the host steps, facing west.

sentences.zh: 禮物陳於庭。

translations.literal: The gifts were displayed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts were displayed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 設席於兩楹間，童子以璽書版升，主人跪受。

translations.literal: A mat was set between the two pillars; a youth ascended with the seal and written tablet; the host knelt to receive.
translations.idiomatic: A mat was set between the two pillars; a youth ascended with the seal and written tablet, and the host knelt to receive.

sentences.zh: 送使者，拜于大門之外。

translations.literal: Seeing off the envoy, he bowed outside the great gate.
translations.idiomatic: To see off the envoy, he bowed outside the great gate.

sentences.zh: 有司先于昭陽殿兩楹間供帳，為同牢之具。

translations.literal: The relevant office had already supplied the pavilion between the two pillars of Zhaoyang Hall with the implements for the shared-mat rite.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office had already supplied the pavilion between the two pillars of Zhaoyang Hall with the implements for the shared-mat rite, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇后服大嚴繡衣，帶綬珮，加幜。

translations.literal: The empress wore the great formal embroidered robe, belt, cord, and pendants, with the veil added.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore the great formal embroidered robe with belt, cord, and pendants, and added the veil.

sentences.zh: 女長禦引出，升畫輪四望車。

translations.literal: The senior lady attendant led her out and helped her ascend the painted four-view carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A senior lady attendant led her out and helped her ascend the painted four-view carriage.

sentences.zh: 女侍中負璽陪乘。

translations.literal: The female attendant-in-ordinary bore the seal and accompanied her in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A female attendant-in-ordinary bore the seal and accompanied her in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿如大駕。

translations.literal: The guard of honor was as for the great procession.
translations.idiomatic: The guard of honor matched that of the great imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕出，升禦坐。

translations.literal: The emperor in dragon robe and crown came out and ascended the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In dragon robe and crown, the emperor robe and crown came out and ascended the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 皇后入門，大鹵簿住門外，小鹵簿入。

translations.literal: When the empress entered the gate, the great guard of honor halted outside the gate; the lesser guard of honor entered.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress entered the gate, the great guard of honor halted outside; the lesser guard of honor entered.

sentences.zh: 到東上閤，施步鄣，降車，席道以入昭陽殿。

translations.literal: Arriving at the Eastern Upper Pavilion, a screen was set; she descended from the carriage, and a mat path was laid to enter Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at the Eastern Upper Pavilion, a screen was set; she descended from the carriage, and a mat path was laid for her to enter Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 前至席位，姆去幜，皇后先拜後起，皇帝後拜先起。

translations.literal: Advancing to the seat, the matron removed the veil; the empress bowed first then rose, the emperor bowed after then rose first.
translations.idiomatic: On advancing to the seat, the matron removed the veil; the empress bowed first then rose, the emperor bowed after then rose first.

sentences.zh: 帝升自西階，詣同牢坐，與皇后俱坐。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the western steps, proceeded to the shared-mat seat, and sat together with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the western steps, the emperor the western steps, proceeded to the shared-mat seat, and sat together with the empress.

sentences.zh: 各三飯訖，又各酳二爵一巹。

translations.literal: Each finished three servings of rice; each also rinsed with two cups and one gourd.
translations.idiomatic: They each finished three servings of rice; each also rinsed with two cups and one gourd.

sentences.zh: 奏禮畢，皇后興，南面立。

translations.literal: When the music for the completed rite was played, the empress rose and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At the music for the completed rite was played, the empress rose and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 皇帝禦太極殿，王公已下拜，皇帝興，入。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the Taichi Hall; the princes and dukes below bowed; the emperor rose and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Proceeding to the Taichi Hall, the emperor to the Taichi Hall; the princes and dukes below bowed; the emperor rose and entered.

sentences.zh: 明日，後展衣，于昭陽殿拜表謝。

translations.literal: The next day the empress in court dress bowed and submitted a memorial of thanks in Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day the empress in court dress bowed and submitted a memorial of thanks in Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 又明日，以榛栗棗修，見皇太后于昭陽殿。

translations.literal: On another day she presented hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat to the Empress Dowager in Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Another day she presented hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat to the Empress Dowager in Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 擇日，群官上禮。

translations.literal: On a chosen day the assembled officials presented congratulatory gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On a selected day the assembled officials presented congratulatory gifts.

sentences.zh: 又擇日謁廟。

translations.literal: On another chosen day she visited the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day she visited the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 皇帝使太尉先乙太牢告，而後遍見群廟。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the Grand Commandant first to report with a single ox at the temple, and afterward to visit all the temples in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Grand Commandant first to report with a single ox at the temple, and afterward to visit all the temples in turn.

sentences.zh: 皇太子納妃禮，皇帝遣使納采，有司備禮物。

translations.literal: For the crown prince taking a consort, the emperor dispatched an envoy for the initial gift; the relevant office prepared the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took a consort, the emperor dispatched an envoy for the initial gift; the relevant office prepared the gifts.

sentences.zh: 會畢，使者受詔而行。

translations.literal: When the banquet was complete, the envoy received the edict and set out.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet was complete, the envoy received the edict and set out.

sentences.zh: 主人迎于大門外。

translations.literal: The host welcomed outside the great gate.
translations.idiomatic: The host welcomed the envoy outside the great gate.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，會於聽事。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, they met in the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, they met in the reception hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 其次問名、納吉，並如納采。

translations.literal: Next came name inquiry and acceptance of auspicious omens, both as at the initial gift.
translations.idiomatic: Next came name inquiry and acceptance of auspicious omens, both following the initial-gift rite.

sentences.zh: 納征，則使司徒及尚書令為使，備禮物而行。

translations.literal: For betrothal gifts, the Minister of Education and Minister of Works served as envoys, with full gifts, and set out.
translations.idiomatic: For betrothal gifts, the Minister of Education and Minister of Works served as envoys, bearing full gifts, and set out.

sentences.zh: 請期，則乙太常宗正卿為使，如納采。

translations.literal: For setting the date, the Director of the Grand Temple and Director of the Imperial Clan served as envoys, as at the initial gift.
translations.idiomatic: Setting the date, the Director of the Grand Temple and Director of the Imperial Clan served as envoys, as at the initial gift.

sentences.zh: 親迎，則太尉為使。

translations.literal: For the personal welcome, the Grand Commandant served as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The personal welcome, the Grand Commandant served as envoy.

sentences.zh: 三日，妃朝皇帝于昭陽殿，又朝皇后于宣光殿。

translations.literal: On the third day the consort attended upon the emperor in Zhaoyang Hall, and upon the empress in Xuangguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the consort attended upon the emperor in Zhaoyang Hall and upon the empress in Xuangguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 擇日，群官上禮。

translations.literal: On a chosen day the assembled officials presented congratulatory gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On a selected day the assembled officials presented congratulatory gifts.

sentences.zh: 他日，妃還。

translations.literal: On another day the consort returned.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the consort returned.

sentences.zh: 又他日，皇太子拜閤。

translations.literal: On yet another day the crown prince paid court at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Still another day the crown prince paid court at the gate.

sentences.zh: 隋皇太子納妃禮，皇帝臨軒，使者受詔而行。

translations.literal: For the Sui crown prince taking a consort, the emperor came to the front hall; the envoy received the edict and set out.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui crown prince taking a consort, the emperor came to the front hall; the envoy received the edict and set out.

sentences.zh: 主人俟于廟。

translations.literal: The host waited at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The host waited at the temple at the temple.

sentences.zh: 使者執雁，主人迎拜于大門之東。

translations.literal: The envoy held the geese; the host welcomed and bowed east of the great gate.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the geese, the envoy the geese; the host welcomed and bowed east of the great gate.

sentences.zh: 使者入，升自西階，立於楹間，南面。

translations.literal: The envoy entered, ascended the western steps, and stood between the pillars facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Entering, the envoy, ascended the western steps, and stood between the pillars facing south.

sentences.zh: 納采訖，乃行問名儀。

translations.literal: When the initial gift was complete, the name inquiry rite was then performed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the initial gift was complete, the name inquiry rite was then performed.

sentences.zh: 事畢，主人請致禮於從者。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the host requested to present gifts to the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the host requested to present gifts to the attendants, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禮有幣馬。

translations.literal: The gifts included silks and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts included silks and horses.

sentences.zh: 其次擇日納吉，如納采。

translations.literal: Next, on a chosen day, auspicious omens were accepted, as at the initial gift.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day next, auspicious omens were accepted, as at the initial gift.

sentences.zh: 又擇日，以玉帛乘馬納征。

translations.literal: On another chosen day, jade silks and horses were sent as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Another chosen day brought jade silks and horses were sent as betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 又擇日告期。

translations.literal: On another chosen day the date was announced.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day the wedding date was announced.

sentences.zh: 又擇日，命有司以特牲告廟，冊妃。

translations.literal: On another chosen day the relevant office was ordered to report to the temple with a special sacrifice and invest the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Another chosen day the relevant office was ordered to report to the temple with a special sacrifice and invest the consort.

sentences.zh: 皇太子將親迎，皇帝臨軒，醮而誡曰：「往迎爾相，承我宗事，勖帥以敬。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was about to welcome her in person, the emperor came to the front hall, offered the parting cup, and admonished him: "Go to meet your partner, uphold our ancestral rites, and lead with reverence."
translations.idiomatic: As the crown prince was about to welcome her in person, the emperor came to the front hall, offered the parting cup, and admonished him: "Go to meet your partner, uphold our ancestral rites, and lead with reverence."

translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied: "I respectfully accept the edict."

sentences.zh: 」既受命，羽儀而行。

translations.literal: Having received the mandate, he set out with guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: With the mandate received the mandate, he set out with guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 主人几筵于廟，妃服褕翟，立于東房。

translations.literal: The host set the offering table at the temple; the consort wore the yu-di robe and stood in the eastern chamber.
translations.idiomatic: At the temple the host set the offering table at the temple; the consort wore the yu-di robe and stood in the eastern chamber.

sentences.zh: 主人迎于門外，西面拜。

translations.literal: The host welcomed outside the gate and bowed facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the great gate, the host welcomed outside the gate and bowed facing west.

sentences.zh: 皇太子答拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince returned the bow, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 主人揖皇太子先入，主人升，立於阼階，西面。

translations.literal: The host bowed and led the crown prince to enter first; the host ascended and stood on the host steps facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The host bowed and led the crown prince to enter first; the host ascended and stood on the host steps facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子升進，當房戶前，北面，跪奠雁，俯伏，興拜，降出。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended and advanced; before the chamber door he faced north, knelt to set down the geese, bowed prostrate, rose, bowed, and descended to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended and advanced; before the chamber door he faced north, knelt to set down the geese, bowed prostrate, rose, bowed, and descended to withdraw, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 妃父少進，西面戒之。

translations.literal: The consort's father stepped forward slightly and admonished her facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The consort's father stepped forward slightly and admonished her facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 母于西階上，施衿結帨，及門內，施鞶申之。

translations.literal: The mother on the western steps placed the collar cord and sash; at the inner gate she placed the purse and applied the sash.
translations.idiomatic: On the western steps the mother the western steps placed the collar cord and sash; at the inner gate she placed the purse and applied the sash.

sentences.zh: 出門，妃升輅，乘以幾。

translations.literal: Going out the gate, the consort ascended the carriage, supported by the armrest.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate going out the gate, the consort ascended the carriage, supported by the armrest.

sentences.zh: 姆加幜。

translations.literal: The matron added the veil.
translations.idiomatic: The matron then added the veil.

sentences.zh: 皇太子乃禦，輪三周，禦者代之。

translations.literal: The crown prince then took the reins; the carriage wheel turned three times, and the driver took over.
translations.idiomatic: Then the crown prince took the reins; the carriage wheel turned three times, and the driver took over.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出大門，乘輅，羽儀還宮。

translations.literal: The crown prince went out the great gate, rode the carriage, and with guard of honor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince then went out the great gate, rode the carriage, and with guard of honor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 妃三日，雞鳴夙興以朝。

translations.literal: On the third day, at cockcrow she rose early to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow on the third day she rose early to attend court.

sentences.zh: 奠檲于皇帝，皇帝撫之。

translations.literal: She presented dried meat to the emperor; the emperor touched it.
translations.idiomatic: She presented dried meat to the emperor, and the emperor touched it.

sentences.zh: 又奠檲于皇后，皇后撫之。

translations.literal: She also presented dried meat to the empress; the empress touched it.
translations.idiomatic: She also presented dried meat to the empress, and the empress touched it.

sentences.zh: 席於戶牖間，妃立于席西，祭奠而出。

translations.literal: A mat was set between the door and window; the consort stood west of the mat, offered the libation, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They set a mat between the door and window; the consort stood west of the mat, offered the libation, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後齊娉禮，一曰納采，二曰問名，三曰納吉，四曰納征，五曰請期，六曰親迎。

translations.literal: The Later Qi betrothal rite: first, initial gift; second, name inquiry; third, acceptance of auspicious omens; fourth, betrothal gifts; fifth, setting the date; sixth, personal welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qi betrothal rite had six stages: initial gift, name inquiry, acceptance of auspicious omens, betrothal gifts, setting the date, and personal welcome.

sentences.zh: 皆用羔羊一口，雁一雙，酒黍稷稻米面各一斛。

translations.literal: All used one lamb, one pair of geese, and one hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour.
translations.idiomatic: All ranks used one lamb, one pair of geese, and one hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour.

sentences.zh: 自皇子王已下至於九品皆同，流外及庶人則減其半。

translations.literal: From imperial princes down to ninth rank all were the same; those outside the regular ranks and commoners had half.
translations.idiomatic: From imperial princes down to ninth rank the gifts were identical; those outside the regular ranks and commoners received half.

sentences.zh: 納征，皇子王用玄三匹，纁二匹，束帛十匹，大璋一第一品已下至從三品，用璧玉，四品已下皆無。

translations.literal: For betrothal gifts, imperial princes used three bolts of black, two bolts of crimson, ten bolts of bundled silk, and one great jade tablet; from first rank down to junior third rank used jade bi; fourth rank and below had none.
translations.idiomatic: For betrothal gifts, imperial princes sent three bolts of black silk, two of crimson, ten of bundled silk, and one great jade tablet. From first rank through junior third rank used jade bi; fourth rank and below had none.

sentences.zh: 獸皮二第一品已下至從五品，用豹皮二，六品已下至從九品，用鹿皮。

translations.literal: Two pieces of animal hide: from first rank down to junior fifth rank used two leopard hides; from sixth rank down to junior ninth rank used deer hide.
translations.idiomatic: Two pieces of animal hide were required: first rank through junior fifth rank used two leopard hides; sixth rank through junior ninth rank used deer hide.

sentences.zh: 錦彩六十匹一品錦彩四十匹，二品三十匹，三品二十匹，四品雜彩十六匹，五品十匹，六品、七品五匹。

translations.literal: Brocade sixty bolts for first rank, forty for second, thirty for third, twenty for fourth, sixteen bolts of mixed colors for fourth rank, ten for fifth, five for sixth and seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade: sixty bolts for first rank, forty for second, thirty for third, twenty for third rank, sixteen bolts of mixed colors for fourth, ten for fifth, five for sixth and seventh.

sentences.zh: 絹二百匹，一品一百四十匹，二品一百二十匹，三品一百匹，四品八十匹，五品六十匹，六品、七品五十匹，八品、九品三十匹。

translations.literal: Silk two hundred bolts: first rank one hundred forty, second one hundred twenty, third one hundred, fourth eighty, fifth sixty, sixth and seventh fifty, eighth and ninth thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Silk totaled two hundred bolts at most: first rank one hundred forty, second one hundred twenty, third one hundred, fourth eighty, fifth sixty, sixth and seventh fifty, eighth and ninth thirty.

sentences.zh: 羔羊一口，羊四口，犢二頭，酒黍稷稻米面各十斛。

translations.literal: One lamb, four sheep, two calves, and ten hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour.
translations.idiomatic: Also one lamb, four sheep, two calves, and ten hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour.

sentences.zh: 一品至三品，減羊二口，酒黍稷稻米面各減六斛，四品、五品減一犢，酒黍稷稻米面又減二斛，六品以下無犢，酒黍稷稻米面各一斛。

translations.literal: First to third rank reduced two sheep and six hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour; fourth and fifth rank reduced one calf and two hu each; sixth rank and below had no calf, one hu each of wine, millet, panicled millet, rice, and flour.
translations.idiomatic: First through third rank reduced two sheep and six hu of each grain and wine; fourth and fifth rank reduced one calf and two hu of each; sixth rank and below had no calf and only one hu of each.

sentences.zh: 諸王之子，已封未封，禮皆同第一品。

translations.literal: Sons of princes, whether enfeoffed or not, all followed first-rank rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of princes, whether enfeoffed or not, all followed first-rank rites, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 新婚從車，皇子百乘，一品五十乘，第二、第三品三十乘，第四、第五品二十乘，第六、第七品十乘，八品達于庶人五乘。

translations.literal: Wedding escort carriages: imperial princes one hundred, first rank fifty, second and third thirty, fourth and fifth twenty, sixth and seventh ten, eighth rank down to commoners five.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding escort carriages numbered one hundred for imperial princes, fifty for first rank, thirty for second and third, twenty for fourth and fifth, ten for sixth and seventh, and five from eighth rank down to commoners.

sentences.zh: 各依其秩之飾。

translations.literal: Each followed the ornamentation of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each followed the ornamentation appropriate to his rank.

sentences.zh: 梁大同五年，臨城公婚，公夫人于皇太子妃為姑侄，進見之制，議者互有不同。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong of Liang, when the Duke of Lincheng married, the duke's wife was aunt to the crown prince's consort; the protocol for the first audience differed among debaters.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Datong 5, when the Duke of Lincheng married, his wife was aunt to the crown prince's consort; debaters disagreed on the protocol for the first audience.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「纁雁之儀，既稱合於二姓，酒食之會，亦有姻不失親。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The crimson-goose rite already marks the union of two surnames; the feast of wine and food also keeps marriage within kinship without losing closeness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The crimson-goose rite already marks the union of two surnames; the feast of wine and food also keeps marriage within kinship without losing closeness, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 若使榛栗潆段修，贄饋必舉，副笄編珈，盛飾斯備，不應婦見之禮，獨以親闕。

translations.literal: If hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat are all presented, secondary hairpins and braided ornaments fully prepared, it is wrong that the bride's audience rite alone should omit kinship on account of relationship.
translations.idiomatic: If hazelnuts, chestnuts, dates, and dried meat are all presented, with secondary hairpins and braided ornaments fully prepared, the bride's audience rite alone should not omit kinship on account of relationship.

sentences.zh: 頃者敬進酏醴，已傳婦事之則，而奉盤沃盥，不行侯服之家。

translations.literal: Recently the respectful presentation of fermented milk and ceremonial wine has already transmitted the rule of wifely duty, yet offering the tray and pouring the hand-washing water is not practiced in marquisate households.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the respectful presentation of fermented milk and ceremonial wine has already transmitted the rule of wifely duty, yet offering the tray and pouring the hand-washing water is not practiced in marquisate households, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 是知繁省不同，質文異世，臨城公夫人于妃既是姑侄，宜停省。」

translations.idiomatic: Thus elaboration and simplification differ, and substance and ornament vary by age. Since the Duke of Lincheng's wife and the consort are aunt and niece, the simplification should cease."

sentences.zh: 後齊將講于天子，先定經于孔父廟，置執經一人，侍講二人，執讀一人，擿句二人，錄義六人，奉經二人。

translations.literal: When Later Qi was about to lecture before the Son of Heaven, the classic was first fixed at the temple of Confucius; one holder of the classic, two lecture attendants, one reader, two phrase-pointers, six recorders of meaning, and two bearers of the classic were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Qi was about to lecture before the Son of Heaven, the classic was first fixed at the temple of Confucius. One holder of the classic, two lecture attendants, one reader, two phrase-pointers, six recorders of meaning, and two bearers of the classic were appointed.

sentences.zh: 講之旦，皇帝服通天冠、玄紗袍，乘象輅，至學，坐廟堂上。

translations.literal: On the morning of the lecture, the emperor wore the tongtian cap and dark gauze robe, rode the elephant carriage to the academy, and sat in the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of the lecture, the emperor wore the tongtian cap and dark gauze robe, rode the elephant carriage to the academy, and sat in the temple hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 講訖，還便殿，改服絳紗袍，乘象輅，還宮。

translations.literal: When the lecture was finished, he returned to the side hall, changed to crimson gauze robe, rode the elephant carriage, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once the lecture was finished, he returned to the side hall, changed to crimson gauze robe, rode the elephant carriage, and returned to the palace, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 講畢，以一太牢釋奠孔父，配以顏回，列軒懸樂，六佾舞。

translations.literal: When the lecture was complete, a single great sacrifice was offered to Confucius, with Yan Hui as associate; suspended bells were arrayed and the six-row dance performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was complete, a single great sacrifice was offered to Confucius with Yan Hui as associate; suspended bells were arrayed and the six-row dance performed.

sentences.zh: 行三獻禮畢，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，升阼，即坐。

translations.literal: When the three offerings were complete, the emperor in tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe ascended the host steps and took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once the three offerings were complete, the emperor in tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe ascended the host steps and took his seat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宴畢，還宮。

translations.literal: When the banquet was complete, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once the banquet was complete, he returned to the palace, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子每通一經，亦釋奠，乘石山安車，三師乘車在前，三少從後而至學焉。

translations.literal: Each time the crown prince mastered a classic he also offered the sacrifice; he rode the stone-mount carriage, the Three Preceptors riding in carriages ahead, the Three Junior Preceptors following behind to the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the crown prince mastered a classic he also offered the sacrifice, riding the stone-mount carriage with the Three Preceptors in carriages ahead and the Three Junior Preceptors following behind to the academy.

sentences.zh: 梁天監八年，皇太子釋奠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian of Liang, the crown prince offered the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Tianjian 8 the crown prince offered the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 周舍議，以為：「釋奠仍會，既惟大禮，請依東宮元會，太子著絳紗襮，樂用軒懸。

translations.literal: Zhou She argued: "The sacrifice is still followed by a banquet — since this is a great rite, please follow the Eastern Palace New Year audience: the crown prince wears the crimson gauze collar-robe, and suspended bells are used.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She argued: "The sacrifice is still followed by a banquet. Since this is a great rite, please follow the Eastern Palace New Year audience: the crown prince wears the crimson gauze collar-robe, and suspended bells are used.

sentences.zh: 預升殿坐者，皆服硃衣。

translations.literal: All who ascend the hall to sit wear vermilion robes.
translations.idiomatic: Every rank who ascend the hall to sit wear vermilion robes, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed, as prescribed.

translations.idiomatic: Relevant office also argued: "The Rites say: 'As a son, one does not ascend or descend by the host steps.'

sentences.zh: '案今學堂凡有三階，愚謂客若降等，則從主人之階。

translations.literal: ' According to the present academy, which has three flights of steps in all, I think that if the guest is of lower rank he follows the host's steps.
translations.idiomatic: According to the present academy, which has three flights of steps, I think that if the guest is of lower rank he follows the host's steps.

sentences.zh: 今先師在堂，義所尊敬，太子宜登阼階，以明從師之義。

translations.literal: Now the former master is in the hall — one whom it is right to honor — so the crown prince should ascend the host steps to make clear the meaning of following the teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Now the former master is in the hall — one whom it is right to honor — so the crown prince should ascend the host steps to make clear the meaning of following the teacher, as prescribed.

translations.idiomatic: If the sacrifice is finished and it is time for the banquet, when there is no longer reverence for the former master, the crown prince ascending the hall should use the western steps to make clear the meaning of not using the host steps, as prescribed.

translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Mian argued: "Zheng Xuan says that from ranked knights upward, father and son dwell in separate quarters."

translations.idiomatic: Since the quarters differ, there is no rule against using the host steps.

translations.literal: I request that for both the sacrifice and the banquet, when the crown prince ascends the hall, he should use the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: I request that for both the sacrifice and the banquet, when the crown prince ascends the hall, he should use the eastern steps, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 若輿駕幸學，自然中陛。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage visits the academy, naturally the central flight is used.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage visits the academy, naturally the central flight is used, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又檢《東宮元會儀注》，太子升崇正殿，不欲東西階。

translations.literal: I also checked the Eastern Palace New Year Audience Protocol: when the crown prince ascends the Chongzheng Hall he does not wish to use the eastern or western steps.
translations.idiomatic: I also checked the Eastern Palace New Year Audience Protocol: when the crown prince ascends the Chongzheng Hall he does not wish to use the eastern or western steps, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 責東宮典儀，列雲：'太子元會，升自西階'，此則相承為謬。

translations.literal: Examining the Eastern Palace master of ceremonies, the list says 'At the crown prince's New Year audience he ascends by the western steps' — this transmitted custom is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Eastern Palace master of ceremonies, the list says "At the crown prince's New Year audience he ascends by the western steps" — this transmitted custom is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 請自今東宮大公事，太子升崇正殿，並由阼階。

translations.literal: I request that from now on, for great affairs of the Eastern Palace, when the crown prince ascends the Chongzheng Hall, he always use the host steps.
translations.idiomatic: I request that from now on, for great affairs of the Eastern Palace, when the crown prince ascends the Chongzheng Hall, he always use the host steps, as prescribed.
