translations.idiomatic: Banquet guests should still use the western steps."

sentences.zh: 大同七年，皇太子表其子甯國、臨城公入學，時議者以與太子有齒胄之義，疑之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, the crown prince memorialized that his sons the Dukes of Ningguo and Lincheng enter the academy; debaters doubted this because of the rule of equal age with the teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 the crown prince memorialized that his sons the Dukes of Ningguo and Lincheng enter the academy; debaters doubted this because of the rule of equal age with the teacher.

sentences.zh: 侍中、尚書令臣敬容、尚書僕射臣纘、尚書臣僧旻、臣之遴、臣筠等，以為：「參、點並事宣尼，回、路同諮泗水，鄒魯稱盛，洙汶無譏。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary and Minister of Works Xiao Jingrong, Vice Minister of Works Liu Zuan, Ministers Xiao Tong, Liu Zilin, and Liu Yun and others argued: "Can and Dian both served Confucius; Hui and Lu both consulted at the Si River — in Zou and Lu this was praised as flourishing, and at Zhu and Wen none scoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary and Minister of Works Xiao Jingrong, Vice Minister Liu Zuan, Ministers Xiao Tong, Liu Zilin, and Liu Yun and others argued: "Can and Dian both served Confucius; Hui and Lu both consulted at the Si River — in Zou and Lu this was praised as flourishing, and at Zhu and Wen none scoffed.

sentences.zh: 師道既光，得一資敬，無虧亞貳，況於兩公，而雲不可？

translations.literal: Since the way of the teacher shines, gaining one measure of reverence does not diminish the heir apparent — how much less for two dukes could one say it is not permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Since the way of the teacher shines, gaining one measure of reverence does not diminish the heir apparent — how much less could one forbid two dukes?

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Permitted."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Permitted."

sentences.zh: 後齊制，新立學，必釋奠禮先聖先師，每歲春秋二仲，常行其禮。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, when a new academy was established, the sacrifice to the former sage and former master was required; each year in the second and eighth months the rite was regularly performed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, when a new academy was established, the sacrifice to the former sage and former master was required; each year in the second and eighth months the rite was regularly performed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 每月旦，祭酒領博士已下及國子諸學生已上，太學、四門博士升堂，助教已下、太學諸生階下，拜孔揖顏。

translations.literal: On the first of each month the libationer led the erudites and below and students of the Directorate of Education and above; erudites of the Grand Academy and Four Gates ascended the hall, assistants and below and Grand Academy students below the steps, bowing to Confucius and bowing to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of each month the libationer led the erudites and below and students of the Directorate of Education and above. Erudites of the Grand Academy and Four Gates ascended the hall; assistants and below and Grand Academy students stood below the steps, bowing to Confucius and bowing to Yan.

sentences.zh: 日出行事而不至者，記之為一負。

translations.literal: Those who did not come on the day of the rite were recorded as one demerit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not come on the day of the rite were recorded as one demerit, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 雨沾服則止。

translations.literal: If rain soaked their clothes the rite was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: If rain soaked their clothes the rite was stopped, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 學生每十日給假，皆以丙日放之。

translations.literal: Students received leave every ten days, always released on bing days.
translations.idiomatic: Students received leave every ten days, always released on bing days, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 郡學則於坊內立孔、顏廟，博士已下，亦每月朝雲。

translations.literal: At the commandery academy temples to Confucius and Yan were set up within the ward; erudites and below also paid court monthly.
translations.idiomatic: At the commandery academy temples to Confucius and Yan were set up within the ward; erudites and below also paid court monthly, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 隋制，國子寺，每歲以四仲月上丁，釋奠於先聖先師。

translations.literal: Under Sui, the Directorate of the Sons of the State each year on the first ding day of the four middle months offered the sacrifice to the former sage and former master.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, the Directorate of the Sons of the State each year on the first ding day of the four middle months offered the sacrifice to the former sage and former master, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 年別一行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: Each year the district drinking rite was performed once.
translations.idiomatic: All year the district drinking rite was performed once, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 州郡學則以春秋仲月釋奠。

translations.literal: Provincial and commandery academies offered the sacrifice in the middle months of spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery academies offered the sacrifice in the middle months of spring and autumn, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣亦每年于學一行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: Provinces, commanderies, and counties also each year performed the district drinking rite at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, and counties also each year performed the district drinking rite at the academy, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 學生皆乙日試書，丙日給假焉。

translations.literal: Students were examined in writing on yi days and given leave on bing days.
translations.idiomatic: Students were examined in writing on yi days and given leave on bing days, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 梁元會之禮，未明，庭燎設，文物充庭。

translations.literal: The Liang New Year audience rite: before dawn, courtyard torches were set and regalia filled the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang New Year audience rite: before dawn, courtyard torches were set and regalia filled the courtyard, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 台門辟，禁衛皆嚴，有司各從其事。

translations.literal: The palace gate opened; the guard was strict; each office attended to its duties.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gate opened; the guard was strict; each office attended to its duties, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 太階東置白獸樽。

translations.literal: East of the great steps the White Beast Vat was placed.
translations.idiomatic: East of the great steps the White Beast Vat was placed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 群臣及諸蕃客並集，各從其班而拜。

translations.literal: The ministers and foreign envoys all assembled, each bowing according to his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and foreign envoys all assembled, each bowing according to his rank, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏中嚴，王公卿尹各執珪璧入拜。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-ordinary reported the second watch; princes, dukes, ministers, and governors each holding jade tablets entered to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary reported the second watch; princes, dukes, ministers, and governors each holding jade tablets entered to bow, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 侍中乃奏外辦，皇帝服袞冕，乘輿以出。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-ordinary then reported that the outer preparations were complete; the emperor in dragon robe and crown rode the palanquin out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary then reported that the outer preparations were complete; the emperor in dragon robe and crown rode the palanquin out, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 侍中扶左，常侍扶右，黃門侍郎一人執曲直華蓋從。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-ordinary supported him on the left, the regular attendant on the right; one vice director of the yellow gate bore the curved and straight canopy and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary supported him on the left, the regular attendant on the right; one vice director of the yellow gate bore the curved and straight canopy and followed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至階，降輿，納舄升坐。

translations.literal: Arriving at the steps, he descended from the palanquin, put on his shoes, and ascended to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at the steps, he descended from the palanquin, put on his shoes, and ascended to sit, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 有司御前施奉珪藉。

translations.literal: The relevant office placed the jade mat before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Relevant office placed the jade mat before the throne, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 王公以下，至阼階，脫舄劍，升殿，席南奉贄珪璧畢，下殿，納舄佩劍，詣本位。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes and below, arriving at the host steps, removed shoes and sword, ascended the hall, south of the mat presented tribute jade and tablets, descended, put on shoes and sword, and went to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes and below, arriving at the host steps, removed shoes and sword, ascended the hall, south of the mat presented tribute jade and tablets, descended, put on shoes and sword, and went to their places, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 主客即徙珪璧於東廂。

translations.literal: The master of guests then moved the jade tablets to the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: Master of guests then moved the jade tablets to the eastern wing, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 帝興，入，徙禦坐於西壁下，東向。

translations.literal: The emperor rose, entered, and moved the imperial seat to below the western wall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor rose, entered, and moved the imperial seat to below the western wall, facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 設皇太子王公已下位。

translations.literal: Places were set for the crown prince, princes, and dukes and below.
translations.idiomatic: Places were set for the crown prince, princes, and dukes and below, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又奏中嚴，皇帝服通天冠，升禦坐。

translations.literal: The second watch was again reported; the emperor in tongtian cap ascended the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Second watch was again reported; the emperor in tongtian cap ascended the imperial seat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 王公上壽禮畢，食。

translations.literal: When the princes and dukes had finished the longevity toast, they ate.
translations.idiomatic: Once the princes and dukes had finished the longevity toast, they ate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 食畢，樂伎奏。

translations.literal: When the meal was finished, musicians performed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the meal was finished, musicians performed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 太宮進禦酒，主書賦黃甘，逮二品已上。

translations.literal: The Grand Provisioner presented imperial wine; the chief secretary distributed yellow citrus, reaching second rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Provisioner presented imperial wine; the chief secretary distributed yellow citrus, reaching second rank and above, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尚書騶騎引計吏，郡國各一人，皆跪受詔。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works's outriders led the accounting clerks — one from each commandery and kingdom — all kneeling to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works's outriders led the accounting clerks — one from each commandery and kingdom — all kneeling to receive the edict, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 侍中讀五條詔，計吏每應諾訖，令陳便宜者，聽詣白獸樽，以次還坐。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-ordinary read the Five Articles Edict; after each accounting clerk answered, those wishing to state useful proposals were permitted to go to the White Beast Vat and then return to their seats in order.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary read the Five Articles Edict; after each accounting clerk answered, those wishing to state useful proposals were permitted to go to the White Beast Vat and then return to their seats in order, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宴樂罷，皇帝乘輿以入。

translations.literal: When the banquet music ended, the emperor rode the palanquin in.
translations.idiomatic: Once the banquet music ended, the emperor rode the palanquin in, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子朝，則遠遊冠服，乘金輅，鹵簿以行。

translations.literal: When the crown prince attended court, he wore the far-wandering cap and robe, rode the golden carriage, and proceeded with guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crown prince attended court, he wore the far-wandering cap and robe, rode the golden carriage, and proceeded with guard of honor, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 預會則劍履升坐。

translations.literal: If attending the banquet he ascended with sword and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: If attending the banquet he ascended with sword and shoes, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 會訖，先興。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he rose first.
translations.idiomatic: Once the banquet ended, he rose first, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 天監六年詔曰：「頃代以來，元日朝畢，次會群臣，則移就西壁下，東向坐。

translations.literal: An edict of the sixth year of Tianjian said: "In recent generations, after the New Year audience was finished and the ministers were convened, the seat was moved to below the western wall, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of Tianjian 6 said: "In recent generations, after the New Year audience was finished and the ministers were convened, the seat was moved to below the western wall, facing east.

sentences.zh: 求之古義，王者宴萬國，唯應南面，何更居東面？

translations.literal: Seeking the ancient meaning, when the king feasts the myriad states he should face only south — why sit facing east?
translations.idiomatic: By ancient meaning, when the king feasts the myriad states he should face only south — why sit facing east?

sentences.zh: 」於是禦坐南向，以西方為上。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the imperial seat faced south, with the west taken as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the imperial seat faced south, with the west taken as the place of honor, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以下，在北壁坐者，悉西邊東向。

translations.literal: The crown prince and those seated on the north wall all sat on the west side facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince and those seated on the north wall all sat on the west side facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尚書令以下在南方坐者，悉東邊西向。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works and those seated on the south all sat on the east side facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and those seated on the south all sat on the east side facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 舊元日禦坐東向，酒壺在東壁下。

translations.literal: Formerly at the New Year the imperial seat faced east, and the wine jar was below the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly at the New Year the imperial seat faced east, and the wine jar was below the eastern wall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禦坐既南向，乃詔壺于南蘭下。

translations.literal: Since the imperial seat now faced south, an edict moved the jar below the southern gallery.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial seat now faced south, an edict moved the jar below the southern gallery, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「元日受五等贄，珪璧並量付所司。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "At the New Year, when receiving tribute of the five ranks, jade tablets and bi disks are all measured and handed to the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "At the New Year, when receiving tribute of the five ranks, jade tablets and bi disks are all measured and handed to the relevant office, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 」周舍案：「《周禮》塚宰，大朝覲，贊玉幣。

translations.literal: " Zhou She noted: "In the Zhou Rites the chief steward assists with jade and silks at the great audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou She noted: "In the Zhou Rites the chief steward assists with jade and silks at the great audience, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尚書，古之塚宰。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is the ancient chief steward.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works is the ancient chief steward, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 頃王者不親撫玉，則不復須塚宰贊助。

translations.literal: In recent times the king does not personally handle the jade, so the chief steward's assistance is no longer needed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the king does not personally handle the jade, so the chief steward's assistance is no longer needed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尋尚書主客曹郎，既塚宰隸職，今元日五等奠玉既竟，請以主客郎受。

translations.literal: Since the director of the host-guest bureau of the Minister of Works is a subordinate office of the chief steward, now that the New Year presentation of jade of the five ranks is finished, I request that the host-guest director receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the director of the host-guest bureau of the Minister of Works is a subordinate office of the chief steward, now that the New Year presentation of jade of the five ranks is finished, I request that the host-guest director receive them, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注《覲禮》雲：'既受之後，出付玉人於外。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates the Audience Rite: 'After receiving them, they are taken out and handed to the jade keeper outside.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan annotates the Audience Rite: "After receiving them, they are taken out and handed to the jade keeper outside.

sentences.zh: '漢時少府，職掌珪璧，請主客受玉，付少府掌。

translations.literal: ' In Han times the privy treasurer managed jade tablets and bi disks; I request that the host-guest director receive the jade and hand it to the privy treasurer for keeping.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the privy treasurer managed jade tablets and bi disks; I request that the host-guest director receive the jade and hand it to the privy treasurer for keeping.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又尚書僕射沈約議：「《正會儀注》，禦出，乘輿至太極殿前，納舄升階。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Shen Yue also argued: "In the Regular Audience Protocol, when the emperor goes out he rides the palanquin to before the Taichi Hall, puts on shoes, and ascends the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Shen Yue also argued: "In the Regular Audience Protocol, when the emperor goes out he rides the palanquin to before the Taichi Hall, puts on shoes, and ascends the steps, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尋路寢之設，本是人君居處，不容自敬宮室。

translations.literal: The setting of the inner chamber is originally the ruler's dwelling — it is not fitting to show reverence to one's own palace.
translations.idiomatic: Setting of the inner chamber is originally the ruler's dwelling — it is not fitting to show reverence to one's own palace, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 案漢氏則乘小車升殿。

translations.literal: According to Han practice, one rode the small carriage to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: According to Han practice, one rode the small carriage to ascend the hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 請自今元正及大公事，禦宜乘小輿至太極階，仍乘版輿升殿。

translations.literal: I request that from now on at the New Year and great public affairs the emperor should ride the small palanquin to the Taichi steps, then ride the platform palanquin to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: I request that from now on at the New Year and great public affairs the emperor should ride the small palanquin to the Taichi steps, then ride the platform palanquin to ascend the hall, as prescribed.

translations.literal: " An edict: "Permitted."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented: "Permitted."

sentences.zh: 陳制，先元會十日，百官並習儀注，令僕已下，悉公服監之。

translations.literal: Under Chen, ten days before the New Year audience all officials rehearsed the protocol; from masters of writing downward all supervised in official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen, ten days before the New Year audience all officials rehearsed the protocol; from masters of writing downward all supervised in official dress, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 設庭燎，街闕、城上、殿前皆嚴兵，百官各設部位而朝。

translations.literal: Courtyard torches were set; street gates, city walls, and before the hall were strictly guarded; officials each took their positions for court.
translations.idiomatic: Courtyard torches were set; street gates, city walls, and before the hall were strictly guarded; officials each took their positions for court, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宮人皆於東堂，隔綺疏而觀。

translations.literal: Palace women were all in the Eastern Hall, viewing through patterned screens.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women were all in the Eastern Hall, viewing through patterned screens, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宮門既無籍，外人但絳衣者，亦得入觀。

translations.literal: Since there was no registry at the palace gate, outsiders in only crimson dress could also enter to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Because there was no registry at the palace gate, outsiders wearing only crimson dress could also enter to watch.

sentences.zh: 是日，上事人發白獸樽。

translations.literal: That day the officer on duty opened the White Beast Vat.
translations.idiomatic: That day the officer on duty opened the White Beast Vat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 自余亦多依梁禮雲。

translations.literal: The rest largely followed Liang rites.
translations.idiomatic: rest largely followed Liang rites, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊正日，侍中宣詔慰勞州郡國使。

translations.literal: On the New Year of Later Qi, the attendant-in-ordinary proclaimed the edict comforting the envoys from provinces, commanderies, and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: On the Later Qi New Year, the attendant-in-ordinary proclaimed the edict comforting envoys from provinces, commanderies, and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 詔牘長一尺三寸，廣一尺，雌黃塗飾，上寫詔書三。

translations.literal: The edict document was one foot three inches long and one foot wide, coated with orpiment, with three copies of the edict written on it.
translations.idiomatic: edict document was one foot three inches long and one foot wide, coated with orpiment, with three copies of the edict written on it, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 計會日，侍中依儀勞郡國計吏，問刺史太守安不，及穀價麥苗善惡，人間疾苦。

translations.literal: On accounting day the attendant-in-ordinary according to the rite comforted the accounting clerks of commanderies and kingdoms, asking whether the governor and prefect were well, and about grain prices, wheat and seedlings, good or bad, and the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On accounting day the attendant-in-ordinary, according to rite, comforted accounting clerks from commanderies and kingdoms, asking whether governors and prefects were well and about grain prices, crops, and the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 又班五條詔書于諸州郡國使人，寫以詔牘一枚，長二尺五寸，廣一尺三寸，亦以雌黃塗飾，上寫詔書。

translations.literal: The Five Articles Edict was also distributed to envoys of all provinces, commanderies, and kingdoms, written on one document one foot five inches long and one foot three inches wide, also coated with orpiment.
translations.idiomatic: Five Articles Edict was also distributed to envoys of all provinces, commanderies, and kingdoms, written on one document one foot five inches long and one foot three inches wide, also coated with orpiment, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 正會日，依儀宣示使人，歸以告刺史二千石。

translations.literal: On the day of the regular audience it was proclaimed to the envoys according to rite; they returned to report to the governors and two-thousand-bushel officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the regular audience it was proclaimed to the envoys according to rite; they returned to report to governors and two-thousand-bushel officials.

sentences.zh: 一曰，政在正身，在愛人，去殘賊，擇良吏，正決獄，平徭賦。

translations.literal: First: governance lies in correcting oneself, in loving the people, in removing cruelty, in selecting good officials, in deciding cases rightly, and in leveling corvée and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: First: governance lies in correcting oneself, loving the people, removing cruelty, selecting good officials, deciding cases rightly, and leveling corvée and taxes.

sentences.zh: 二曰，人生在勤，勤則不匱，其勸率田桑，無或煩擾。

translations.literal: Second: human life depends on diligence — if diligent one is not in want; encourage and lead field and mulberry, and do not harass.
translations.idiomatic: Second: human life depends on diligence; if diligent one is not in want. Encourage field and mulberry work and do not harass the people.

sentences.zh: 三曰，六極之人，務加寬養，必使生有以自救，沒有以自給。

translations.literal: Third: the six extremes of misfortune — see that they receive generous care, so that in life they have means to save themselves and in death means for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Third: for those in the six extremes of misfortune, ensure generous care so that in life they can save themselves and in death have means for burial.

sentences.zh: 四曰，長吏華浮，奉客以求小譽，逐末舍本，政之所疾，宜謹察之。

translations.literal: Fourth: long officials who are flashy, entertaining guests to win small praise, pursuing the branch and abandoning the root — this is what government should punish; examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: long-serving officials who are flashy, entertaining guests for small praise and pursuing the branch while abandoning the root — this government should punish; examine it carefully.

sentences.zh: 五曰，人事意氣，幹亂奉公，外內溷淆，綱紀不設，所宜糾劾。

translations.literal: Fifth: personal feelings and arrogance that disrupt public service, confusion inside and out, failure to set standards — this should be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: personal feelings and arrogance that disrupt public service, confusion inside and out, and failure to set standards — this should be impeached.

sentences.zh: 正會日，侍中黃門宣詔勞諸郡上計。

translations.literal: On the day of the regular audience the attendant-in-ordinary and yellow gate proclaimed the edict comforting the accounting clerks of all commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the regular audience the attendant-in-ordinary and yellow gate proclaimed the edict comforting accounting clerks of all commanderies.

sentences.zh: 勞訖付紙，遣陳土宜。

translations.literal: When the comfort was finished they were given paper and ordered to describe local conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Once the comfort was finished they were given paper and ordered to describe local conditions, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 字有脫誤者，呼起席後立。

translations.literal: If characters were missing or wrong they were called to stand behind their seats.
translations.idiomatic: Where characters were missing or wrong they were called to stand behind their seats, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 書跡濫劣者，飲墨水一升。

translations.literal: If handwriting was sloppy and poor they drank one sheng of ink.
translations.idiomatic: If handwriting was sloppy and poor they were made to drink one sheng of ink.

sentences.zh: 文理孟浪無可取者，奪容刀及席。

translations.literal: If the writing was careless and worthless, their ceremonial knife and seat were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Where the writing was careless and worthless, their ceremonial knife and seat were taken, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 即而本曹郎中考其文跡才辭可聚者，錄牒吏部，簡同流外三品敘。

translations.literal: Then the clerks of the relevant bureau examined those whose writing and talent were acceptable, recorded them for the Ministry of Personnel, and selected them for appointment outside the regular ranks at third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Then clerks of the relevant bureau examined those whose writing and talent were acceptable, recorded them for the Ministry of Personnel, and selected them for appointment outside the regular ranks at third grade.

sentences.zh: 元正大饗，百官一品已下，流外九品已上預會。

translations.literal: At the New Year great feast, officials from first rank down and from outside the nine ranks up to outside the nine ranks down attended.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year great feast, officials from first rank down and from outside the nine ranks up attended.

sentences.zh: 一品已下、正三品已上、開國公侯伯、散品公侯及特命之官、下代刺史，並升殿。

translations.literal: First rank down, regular third rank up, founding dukes, marquises, and earls, honorary dukes and marquises, and specially appointed officials and former-generation governors all ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: From first rank down through regular third rank up, founding dukes, marquises, and earls, honorary dukes and marquises, specially appointed officials, and former-generation governors all ascended the hall.

sentences.zh: 從三品已下、從九品以上及奉正使人比流官者，在階下。

translations.literal: Junior third rank down, junior ninth rank up, and envoys of tribute states comparable to outside-rank officials stood below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Junior third rank down through junior ninth rank up, and envoys of tribute states comparable to outside-rank officials, stood below the steps.

sentences.zh: 勳品已下端門外。

translations.literal: Meritorious ranks of lowest grade stood outside the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ranks of the lowest grade stood outside the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 隋制，正旦及冬至，文物充庭，皇帝出西房，即御座。

translations.literal: Under Sui, at the New Year and winter solstice regalia filled the courtyard; the emperor came out from the western chamber and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, at the New Year and winter solstice regalia filled the courtyard; the emperor came out from the western chamber and took the imperial seat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子鹵簿至顯陽門外，入賀。

translations.literal: The crown prince's guard of honor reached outside the Xianyang Gate; he entered to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: crown prince's guard of honor reached outside the Xianyang Gate; he entered to offer congratulations, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 複詣皇后禦殿，拜賀訖，還宮。

translations.literal: He again proceeded to the empress's hall, bowed in congratulation, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again proceeded to the empress's hall, bowed in congratulation, and returned to the palace, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子朝訖，群官客使入就位，再拜。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's audience was finished, assembled officials and envoys took their places and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crown prince's audience was finished, assembled officials and envoys took their places and bowed twice, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 上公一人，詣西階，解劍，升賀；

translations.literal: One senior duke proceeded to the western steps, removed his sword, ascended to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: One senior duke proceeded to the western steps, removed his sword, and ascended to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 降階，帶劍，復位而拜。

translations.literal: He descended the steps, girded his sword, returned to his place, and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended the steps, girded his sword, returned to his place, and bowed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諸州表。

translations.literal: The relevant office reported memorials from all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: relevant office reported memorials from all provinces, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 群官在位者又拜而出。

translations.literal: Assembled officials in their places bowed again and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Assembled officials in their places bowed again and withdrew, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入東房，有司奏行事訖，乃出西房。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the eastern chamber; the relevant office reported the rite finished; he then came out from the western chamber.
translations.idiomatic: emperor entered the eastern chamber; the relevant office reported the rite finished; he then came out from the western chamber, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 坐定，群官入就位，上壽訖，上下俱拜。

translations.literal: When seated, assembled officials entered to their places; when the longevity toast was finished, upper and lower all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, assembled officials entered to their places; when the longevity toast was finished, upper and lower all bowed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝舉酒，上下舞蹈，三稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The emperor raised his cup; upper and lower danced and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: emperor raised his cup; upper and lower danced and thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 皇太子預會，則設坐于禦東南，西向。

translations.literal: If the crown prince attended, a seat was set southeast of the throne, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Where the crown prince attended, a seat was set southeast of the throne, facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 群臣上壽畢，入，解劍以升。

translations.literal: When the ministers had finished the longevity toast, he entered, removed his sword, and ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ministers had finished the longevity toast, he entered, removed his sword, and ascended, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 會訖，先興。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, he rose first.
translations.idiomatic: Once the banquet ended, he rose first, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊元日，中宮朝會，陳樂，皇后褘衣乘輿，以出於昭陽殿。

translations.literal: On the New Year of Later Qi, the inner palace held court; music was performed; the empress in hui robe rode the palanquin out from Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the Later Qi New Year the inner palace held court; music was performed; the empress in hui robe rode the palanquin out from Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 坐定，內外命婦拜，皇后興，妃主皆跪。

translations.literal: When seated, inner and outer titled ladies bowed; the empress rose and consorts and princesses all knelt.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, inner and outer titled ladies bowed; the empress rose and consorts and princesses all knelt, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇后坐，妃主皆起，長公主一人，前跪拜賀。

translations.literal: When the empress seated herself, consorts and princesses all rose; one senior princess advanced and knelt in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress seated herself, consorts and princesses all rose; one senior princess advanced and knelt in congratulation, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，皇后入室，乃移幄坐於西廂。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete the empress entered her chamber and moved the canopy seat to the western wing.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rite was complete the empress entered her chamber and moved the canopy seat to the western wing, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇后改服褕狄以出。

translations.literal: The empress changed to the yu-di robe and came out.
translations.idiomatic: empress changed to the yu-di robe and came out, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 坐定，公主一人上壽訖，就坐。

translations.literal: When one princess had finished the longevity toast she took her seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once one princess had finished the longevity toast she took her seat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禦酒食，賜爵，並如外朝會。

translations.literal: Imperial wine and food were served; cups were bestowed — all as at the outer court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial wine and food were served and cups bestowed — all as at the outer court audience.

sentences.zh: 隋儀如後齊制，而又有皇后受群臣賀禮。

translations.literal: The Sui rite followed the Later Qi system, but also had the rite of the empress receiving congratulations from ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui rite followed the Later Qi system, but also included the empress receiving congratulations from ministers.

sentences.zh: 則皇后禦坐，而內侍受群臣拜以入，承令而出，群臣拜而罷。

translations.literal: Then the empress took the imperial seat; inner attendants received the ministers' bows and entered; bearing the command they came out; the ministers bowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress took the imperial seat; inner attendants received the ministers' bows and entered; bearing the command they came out; the ministers bowed and withdrew, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊皇太子月五朝。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi the crown prince attended court five times a month.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi the crown prince attended court five times a month, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 未明二刻，乘小輿出，為三師降。

translations.literal: Two quarters before dawn he rode the small palanquin out, descending for the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: Two quarters before dawn he rode the small palanquin out, descending for the Three Preceptors, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至承華門，升石山安車，三師軺車在前，三少在後，自雲龍門入。

translations.literal: At Chenghua Gate he mounted the stone-mount carriage; the Three Preceptors' light carriages went ahead, the Three Junior Preceptors behind; he entered by the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Chenghua Gate he mounted the stone-mount carriage; the Three Preceptors' light carriages went ahead, the Three Junior Preceptors behind; he entered by the Cloud Dragon Gate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝禦殿前，設拜席位，至柏閣，齋帥引，洗馬、中庶子從。

translations.literal: The emperor was before the hall; bowing mats were set; at the Cypress Pavilion the director of fasts led, the groom of the heir and junior tutor following.
translations.idiomatic: emperor was before the hall; bowing mats were set; at the Cypress Pavilion the director of fasts led, the groom of the heir and junior tutor following, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至殿前席南，北面再拜。

translations.literal: Arriving south of the hall mat he faced north and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving south of the hall mat he faced north and bowed twice, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，皇太子監國，在西林園冬會。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao the crown prince supervised the state and held a winter assembly in the Western Grove Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the crown prince supervised the state and held a winter assembly in the Western Grove Garden.

sentences.zh: 群議皆東面。

translations.literal: The assembled debaters all faced east.
translations.idiomatic: assembled debaters all faced east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 二年，於北城第內冬會，又議東面。

translations.literal: In the second year at a winter assembly in the northern city residence, they again debated facing east.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year at a winter assembly in the northern city residence, they again debated facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎陸卬疑非禮，魏收改為西面。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Ang doubted this was not ritual; Wei Shou changed it to facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Ang doubted this was not ritual; Wei Shou changed it to facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 邢子才議欲依前，曰：

translations.literal: Xing Zicai argued for the previous practice, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai spoke in favor of the previous practice, saying:

sentences.zh: 凡禮有同者，不可令異。

translations.literal: Where rites are the same, they cannot be made different.
translations.idiomatic: Where rites are the same, they cannot be made different, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 《詩》說，天子至於大夫，皆乘四馬，況以方面之少，何可皆不同乎？

translations.literal: The Odes say that from the Son of Heaven down to the grandee all ride four horses — how much less can all differ because the area is small?
translations.idiomatic: Odes say that from the Son of Heaven down to the grandee all ride four horses — how much less can all differ because the area is small?

sentences.zh: 若太子定西面者，王公卿大夫士，複何面邪？

translations.literal: If the crown prince is fixed facing west, what direction should princes, dukes, ministers, grandees, and knights face?
translations.idiomatic: Where the crown prince is fixed facing west, what direction should princes, dukes, ministers, grandees, and knights face?

sentences.zh: 南面人君正位，今一官之長，無不南面，太子聽政，亦南面坐。

translations.literal: Facing south is the ruler's proper place; today no head of an office fails to face south, and the crown prince hearing cases also sits facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Facing south is the ruler's proper place; today no head of an office fails to face south, and the crown prince hearing cases also sits facing south, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 議者言皆晉舊事，太子在東宮西面，為避尊位，非為向台殿也。

translations.literal: Debaters say all this follows Jin custom — the crown prince in the Eastern Palace faced west to avoid the honored place, not to face the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters say all this follows Jin custom — the crown prince in the Eastern Palace faced west to avoid the honored place, not to face the hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 子才以為東晉博議，依漢、魏之舊，太子普臣四海，不以為嫌，又何疑於東面？

translations.literal: Zicai thought the Eastern Jin broad debate followed Han and Wei custom; the crown prince is minister to all within the seas and does not take this as objectionable — why doubt facing east?
translations.idiomatic: Zicai held that the Eastern Jin broad debate followed Han and Wei custom; the crown prince is minister to all within the seas and does not take this as objectionable — why doubt facing east?

sentences.zh: 《禮》「世子絕旁親」，「世子冠於阼」，「塚子生，接乙太牢」。

translations.literal: The Rites: "The heir apparent cuts off collateral kin," "the heir apparent is capped at the host steps," "when the eldest son is born, a single ox is offered."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "The heir apparent cuts off collateral kin," "the heir apparent is capped at the host steps," "when the eldest son is born, a single ox is offered."

sentences.zh: 漢元著令，太子絕馳道。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han established the rule that the crown prince cut off the imperial roadway.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han established the rule that the crown prince cut off the imperial roadway, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 此皆禮同於君。

translations.literal: All these make ritual the same as for the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Every these make ritual the same as for the ruler, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又晉王公世子，攝命臨國，乘七旒安車，駕用三馬，禮同三公。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin princes and dukes' heirs, acting on command to govern the state, rode the seven-tassel secure carriage with three horses — ritual the same as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Further, Jin princes and dukes' heirs, acting on command to govern the state, rode the seven-tassel secure carriage with three horses — ritual the same as the Three Dukes, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 近宋太子乘象輅，皆有同處，不以為嫌。

translations.literal: Recently the Song crown prince rode the elephant carriage — there are shared points and none took this as objectionable.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Song crown prince rode the elephant carriage — there are shared points and none took this as objectionable, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 況東面者，君臣通禮，獨何為避？

translations.literal: Moreover facing east is the rite common to minister and ruler — why alone avoid it?
translations.idiomatic: Further, facing east is the rite common to minister and ruler — why alone avoid it?

sentences.zh: 明為向台，所以然也。

translations.literal: Clearly it is to face the hall — that is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly it is to face the hall — that is the reason, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 近皇太子在西林園，在於殿猶且東面，於北城非宮殿之處，更不得邪？

translations.literal: Recently the crown prince in the Western Grove Garden, though still in a hall, yet faced east; in the northern city, not a palace place, could it be otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Recently in the Western Grove Garden, though still in a hall, the crown prince yet faced east; in the northern city, not a palace place, could it be otherwise?

sentences.zh: 諸人以東面為尊，宴會須避。

translations.literal: Debaters say facing east is honored and at banquets one must yield.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters say facing east is honored and at banquets one must yield, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 案《燕禮》、《燕義》，君位在東，賓位則在西，君位在阼階，故有《武王踐阼篇》，不在西也。

translations.literal: According to the Banquet Rite and Meaning of the Banquet, the host's place is east and the guest's west; the host's place is on the host steps — hence the chapter "King Wu Ascends the Steps," not on the west.
translations.idiomatic: By to the Banquet Rite and Meaning of the Banquet, the host's place is east and the guest's west; the host's place is on the host steps — hence the chapter "King Wu Ascends the Steps," not on the west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 《禮》「乘君之車，不敢曠左」。

translations.literal: The Rites: "Riding the ruler's carriage, one dare not leave the left side empty."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: "Riding the ruler's carriage, one dare not leave the left side empty."

sentences.zh: 君在，惡空其位，左亦在東，不在西也。

translations.literal: When the ruler is present one dislikes leaving his place empty; the left is also east, not west.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ruler is present one dislikes leaving his place empty; the left is also east, not west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 「君在阼，夫人在房」。

translations.literal: "The ruler is on the host steps, the lady is in the inner chamber."
translations.idiomatic: The text says: "The ruler is on the host steps, the lady is in the inner chamber."

sentences.zh: 鄭注「人君尊東也」。

translations.literal: Zheng's annotation: "The ruler honors the east."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng annotates: "The ruler honors the east."

sentences.zh: 前代及今，皇帝宴會接客，亦東堂西面。

translations.literal: In former ages and now, when the emperor feasts and receives guests he also sits in the eastern hall facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In former ages and now, when the emperor feasts and receives guests he also sits in the eastern hall facing west, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 若以東面為貴，皇太子以儲後之禮，監國之重，別第宴臣賓，自得申其正位。

translations.literal: If facing east is honored, the crown prince by the rite of the heir and the weight of supervising the state, feasting ministers and guests at a separate residence, may properly assert his correct place.
translations.idiomatic: Where facing east is honored, the crown prince by the rite of the heir and the weight of supervising the state, feasting ministers and guests at a separate residence, may properly assert his correct place, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 禮者皆東宮臣屬，公卿接宴，觀禮而已。

translations.literal: In ritual all are Eastern Palace subordinates; when dukes and ministers join the feast they only observe the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual all are Eastern Palace subordinates; when dukes and ministers join the feast they only observe the rite, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 若以西面為卑，實是君之正位。

translations.literal: If facing west is lowly, in truth it is the ruler's proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Where facing west is lowly, in truth it is the ruler's proper place, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 太公不肯北面說《丹書》，西面則道之，西面乃尊也。

translations.literal: Taigong would not speak the Red Book facing north — facing west then he expounded the Way; facing west is thus honored.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong would not speak the Red Book facing north — facing west then he expounded the Way; facing west is thus honored, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 君位南面，有東有西，何可皆避？

translations.literal: The ruler's place faces south; there is east and there is west — how can all yield?
translations.idiomatic: ruler's place faces south; there is east and there is west — how can all yield?

sentences.zh: 且事雖少異，有可相比者。

translations.literal: Moreover though affairs differ slightly, there are points that can be compared.
translations.idiomatic: Further, though affairs differ slightly, there are points that can be compared, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 周公，臣也，太子，子也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a minister; the crown prince is a son.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhou was a minister; the crown prince is a son, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 周公為塚宰，太子為儲貳。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was chief steward; the crown prince is heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhou was chief steward; the crown prince is heir apparent, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 明堂尊於別第，朝諸侯重于宴臣賓，南面貴於東面。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is more honored than a separate residence; receiving the feudal lords is weightier than feasting ministers and guests; facing south is more honored than facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall is more honored than a separate residence; receiving the feudal lords is weightier than feasting ministers and guests; facing south is more honored than facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 臣疏於子，塚宰輕于儲貳。

translations.literal: The minister is more distant than the son; the chief steward is lighter than the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: minister is more distant than the son; the chief steward is lighter than the heir apparent, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 周公攝政，得在明堂南面朝諸侯。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou as regent could stand in the Bright Hall facing south to receive the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhou as regent could stand in the Bright Hall facing south to receive the feudal lords, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 今太子監國，不得於別第異宮東面宴客，情所未安。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince supervising the state cannot at a separate residence in a different palace feast guests facing east — the feeling is not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince supervising the state cannot at a separate residence in a different palace feast guests facing east — the feeling is not at ease, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 且君行以太子監國，君宴不以公卿為賓，明父子無嫌，君臣有嫌。

translations.literal: Moreover when the ruler travels the crown prince supervises the state; when the ruler feasts he does not take dukes and ministers as guests — clearly father and son have no suspicion, but minister and ruler do.
translations.idiomatic: Further, when the ruler travels the crown prince supervises the state; when the ruler feasts he does not take dukes and ministers as guests — clearly father and son have no suspicion, but minister and ruler do, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 案《儀注》，親王受詔冠婚，皇子皇女皆東面。

translations.literal: According to the Protocol, when imperial princes receive the edict for capping or marriage, imperial sons and daughters all face east.
translations.idiomatic: By to the Protocol, when imperial princes receive the edict for capping or marriage, imperial sons and daughters all face east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 今不約王公南面，而獨約太子，何所取邪？

translations.literal: Now without restricting princes and dukes to facing south, yet restricting only the crown prince — what is taken from this?
translations.idiomatic: Now without restricting princes and dukes to facing south, yet restricting only the crown prince — what principle is taken from this?

sentences.zh: 議者南尊改就西面，轉君位，更非合禮。

translations.literal: Debaters changed from honoring the south to facing west, turning the ruler's place — this is even less in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters changed from honoring the south to facing west, turning the ruler's place — this is even less in accord with ritual, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 方面既少，難為節文。

translations.literal: Since directions are few, it is hard to regulate the text.
translations.idiomatic: Since directions are few, it is hard to regulate the text, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 東西二面，君臣通用，太子宜然，於禮為允。

translations.literal: East and west are both used by minister and ruler; the crown prince should be so — in ritual this is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: East and west are both used by minister and ruler; the crown prince should be so — in ritual this is acceptable, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 魏收議雲：

translations.literal: Wei Shou argued:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou countered:

sentences.zh: 去天保初，皇太子監國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao the crown prince supervised the state.
translations.idiomatic: During the beginning of Tianbao the crown prince supervised the state, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 冬會群官於西園都亭，坐從東面，義取于向中宮台殿故也。

translations.literal: At the winter assembly of officials in the Western Garden Pavilion he sat facing east, taking the meaning of facing the inner palace and hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the winter assembly of officials in the Western Garden Pavilion he sat facing east, taking the meaning of facing the inner palace and hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 二年于宮冬會，坐乃東面，收竊以為疑。

translations.literal: In the second year at the winter assembly in the palace he sat facing east; Shou privately found this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year at the winter assembly in the palace he sat facing east; Shou privately found this doubtful, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 前者遂有別議，議者同之。

translations.literal: Earlier there was a separate debate; the debaters agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was a separate debate; the debaters agreed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 邢尚書以前定東面之議，複申本懷，此乃國之大禮，無容不盡所見。

translations.literal: Minister Xing, based on the earlier fixed east-facing decision, again stated his original view — this is a great state rite and cannot but fully express one's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xing, based on the earlier fixed east-facing decision, again stated his original view — this is a great state rite and one cannot withhold one's full opinion.

sentences.zh: 收以為太子東宮，位在於震，長子之義也。

translations.literal: Shou thought the crown prince's Eastern Palace is placed in the Zhen trigram — the meaning of the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Shou thought the crown prince's Eastern Palace is placed in the Zhen trigram — the meaning of the eldest son, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 案《易》八卦，正位向中。

translations.literal: According to the eight trigrams of the Changes, the proper position faces the center.
translations.idiomatic: By to the eight trigrams of the Changes, the proper position faces the center, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子今居北城，于宮殿為東北，南面而坐，於義為背也。

translations.literal: The crown prince now dwells in the northern city; relative to the palace he is northeast — sitting facing south is in meaning turning one's back.
translations.idiomatic: crown prince now dwells in the northern city; relative to the palace he is northeast — sitting facing south is in meaning turning one's back, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 前者立議，據東宮為本。

translations.literal: The earlier decision was based on the Eastern Palace as foundation.
translations.idiomatic: earlier decision was based on the Eastern Palace as foundation, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又案《東宮舊事》，太子宴會，多以西面為禮，此又成證，非徒言也。

translations.literal: I also checked the Old Affairs of the Eastern Palace: at crown prince banquets facing west was mostly the rite — this is further proof, not mere words.
translations.idiomatic: Shou also checked the Old Affairs of the Eastern Palace: at crown prince banquets facing west was mostly the rite — this is further proof, not mere words, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 不言太子常無東南二面之坐，但用之有所。

translations.literal: I do not say the crown prince never sits southeast or southwest — only that each is used where appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Shou do not say the crown prince never sits southeast or southwest — only that each is used where appropriate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 至如西園東面，所不疑也。

translations.literal: As for the Western Garden facing east, there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Western Garden facing east, there is no doubt, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 未知君臣車服有同異之議，何為而發？

translations.literal: I do not know what debate about sameness or difference in carriage and dress of minister and ruler prompted this — why was it raised?
translations.idiomatic: Shou do not know what debate about sameness or difference in carriage and dress of minister and ruler prompted this — why was it raised?

sentences.zh: 就如所雲，但知禮有同者，不可令異。

translations.literal: Even as they say, one only knows that where ritual is the same it cannot be made different.
translations.idiomatic: Even as they say, one only knows that where ritual is the same it cannot be made different, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 不知禮有異者，不可令同。

translations.literal: One does not know that where ritual differs it cannot be made the same.
translations.idiomatic: One does not know that where ritual differs it cannot be made the same, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 苟別君臣同異之禮，恐重紙累劄，書不盡也。

translations.literal: If one distinguished the rites of sameness and difference between minister and ruler, I fear the paper would pile up and writing would not exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: Where one distinguished the rites of sameness and difference between minister and ruler, I fear the paper would pile up and writing would not exhaust it, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 子才竟執東面，收執西面，授引經據，大相往復。

translations.literal: Zicai finally held to east; Shou held to west — citing classics back and forth at great length.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai finally held to east; Shou held to west — citing classics back and forth at great length, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 其後竟從西面為定。

translations.literal: In the end facing west was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end facing west was fixed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 時議又疑宮吏之姓與太子名同。

translations.literal: At the time debaters also doubted whether a palace officer's surname was the same as the crown prince's name.
translations.idiomatic: During the time debaters also doubted whether a palace officer's surname was the same as the crown prince's name, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 子才又謂曰：「案《曲禮》'大夫士之子，不與世子同名。

translations.literal: Zicai also said: "According to the Court Rites, 'sons of grandees and knights do not share the heir apparent's name.'
translations.idiomatic: Zicai also said: "According to the Court Rites, sons of grandees and knights do not share the heir apparent's name."

sentences.zh: '《鄭注》雲：'若先之生，亦不改。

translations.literal: Zheng's annotation says: 'If born first, it is also not changed.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's annotation says: "If born first, it is also not changed."

sentences.zh: '漢法，天子登位，布名于天下，四海之內，無不鹹避。

translations.literal: Han law: when the Son of Heaven acceded he published his name throughout the realm — within the four seas none failed to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Han law: when the Son of Heaven acceded he published his name throughout the realm — within the four seas none failed to avoid it, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 案《春秋經》'衛石惡出奔晉'，在衛侯衎卒之前。

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, "Wei's Shi E fled to Jin" — before Duke Xian of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: By to the Spring and Autumn Annals, "Wei's Shi E fled to Jin" — before Duke Xian of Wei died, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 衎卒，其子惡始立。

translations.literal: When Xian died his son E was first installed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xian died his son E was first installed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 明石惡于長子同名。

translations.literal: This shows Shi E shared the eldest son's name.
translations.idiomatic: This shows Shi E shared the eldest son's name, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 諸侯長子，在一國之內，與皇太子于天子，禮亦不異。

translations.literal: The feudal lords' eldest sons, within one state, and the crown prince relative to the Son of Heaven — ritual is not different.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords' eldest sons within one state, and the crown prince relative to the Son of Heaven — ritual is not different.

sentences.zh: 鄭言先生不改，蓋以此義。

translations.literal: Zheng's saying that those born first are not changed probably takes this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's saying that those born first are not changed probably takes this meaning, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 衛石惡、宋向戌皆與君同名，《春秋》不譏。

translations.literal: Wei's Shi E and Song's Xiang Xu both shared their ruler's name — the Spring and Autumn does not censure them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Shi E and Song's Xiang Xu both shared their ruler's name — the Spring and Autumn does not censure them, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇太子雖有儲貳之重，未為海內所避，何容便改人姓。

translations.literal: Though the crown prince has the weight of heir apparent, he is not yet avoided throughout the realm — how can one lightly change people's surnames?
translations.idiomatic: Though the crown prince bears the weight of heir apparent, he is not yet taboo throughout the realm — how can one lightly change people's surnames?

sentences.zh: 然事有消息，不得皆同于古。

translations.literal: Yet affairs have their fluctuations and cannot all match antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs have their fluctuations and cannot all match antiquity, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宮吏至微，而有所犯，朝夕從事，亦是難安，宜聽出宮，尚書更補他職。

translations.literal: Palace officers are most lowly, yet if they violate this and attend morning and evening it is also hard to be at ease — they should be permitted to leave the palace; the Ministry of Works should replace them with others.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers are most lowly, yet if they violate this and attend morning and evening it is also hard to be at ease — they should be permitted to leave the palace; the Ministry of Works should replace them with others, as prescribed.

translations.literal: " An edict: "Permitted."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented: "Permitted."

sentences.zh: 後周制，正之二日，皇太子南面，列軒懸，宮官朝賀。

translations.literal: Under Later Zhou, on the second day of the first month the crown prince faced south, suspended bells were arrayed, and palace officers offered New Year congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou, on the second day of the first month the crown prince faced south, suspended bells were arrayed, and palace officers offered New Year congratulations, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 及開皇初，皇太子勇准故事，張樂受朝，宮臣及京官北面稱慶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Crown Prince Yong followed precedent, spread music, and received court; palace officers and capital officials faced north and shouted congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: During the beginning of Kaihuang, Crown Prince Yong followed precedent, spread music, and received court; palace officers and capital officials faced north and shouted congratulations, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 高祖誚之。

translations.literal: Gaozu reproved this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu reproved this, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 是後定儀注，西面而坐，唯宮臣稱慶，台官不復總集。

translations.literal: Afterward the protocol was fixed: sitting facing west, only palace officers shouted congratulations; capital officials no longer all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the protocol was fixed: sitting facing west, only palace officers shouted congratulations; capital officials no longer all assembled, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝之為太子，奏降章服，宮官請不稱臣。

translations.literal: When Yang Guang was crown prince he memorialized to reduce his robe rank; palace officers requested not to address him as "subject."
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Guang was crown prince he memorialized to reduce his robe rank; palace officers requested not to address him as "subject."

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor permitted it, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊立春日，皇帝服通天冠、青介幘、青紗袍，佩蒼玉，青帶、青袴、青襪舄，而受朝於太極殿。

translations.literal: On the Beginning of Spring of Later Qi, the emperor wore the tongtian cap, green headband cap, green gauze robe, dark jade pendant, green belt, green trousers, green socks and shoes, and received court in the Taichi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Beginning of Spring of Later Qi, the emperor wore the tongtian cap, green headband cap, green gauze robe, dark jade pendant, green belt, green trousers, green socks and shoes, and received court in the Taichi Hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尚書令等坐定，三公郎中詣席，跪讀時令訖，典禦酌酒卮，置郎中前，郎中耑，還席伏飲，禮成而出。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Works and others were seated, a director of the Three Dukes bureau came to the mat, knelt, read the seasonal command, finished; the imperial caterer poured wine into a cup, placed it before the director, who drank alone, returned to his seat, bowed prostrate, drank, and when the rite was complete withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister of Works and others were seated, a director of the Three Dukes bureau came to the mat, knelt, and read the seasonal command. The imperial caterer poured wine into a cup, placed it before the director, who drank alone, returned to his seat, bowed prostrate, drank, and when the rite was complete withdrew.

sentences.zh: 立夏、季夏、立秋讀令，則施御座於中楹，南向。

translations.literal: For Beginning of Summer, Midsummer, and Beginning of Autumn command-reading, the imperial seat was set at the central pillar facing south.
translations.idiomatic: For Beginning of Summer, Midsummer, and Beginning of Autumn command-reading, the imperial seat was set at the central pillar facing south, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 立冬如立春，於西廂東向。

translations.literal: Beginning of Winter was as Beginning of Spring, in the western wing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning of Winter was as Beginning of Spring, in the western wing facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 各以其時之色服，儀並如春禮。

translations.literal: Each used robes of the color of the season; the rite was all as at the spring rite.
translations.idiomatic: Each used robes of the color of the season; the rite was all as at the spring rite, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊每策秀孝，中書策秀才，集書策考貢士，考功郎中策廉良，皇帝常服，乘輿出，坐於朝堂中楹。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, whenever licentiates and filial exemplars were examined, the Secretariat examined licentiates, the Directorate examined tribute scholars, the Director of Merit examined the incorrupt and able; the emperor in regular dress rode the palanquin out and sat at the central pillar of the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, whenever licentiates and filial exemplars were examined, the Secretariat examined licentiates, the Directorate examined tribute scholars, the Director of Merit examined the incorrupt and able; the emperor in regular dress rode the palanquin out and sat at the central pillar of the court hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 秀孝各以班草對。

translations.literal: Licentiates and filial exemplars each answered in turn with draft essays.
translations.idiomatic: Licentiates and filial exemplars each answered in turn with draft essays, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 其有脫誤、書濫、孟浪者，起立席後，飲墨水，脫容刀。

translations.literal: Those with omissions, sloppy writing, or carelessness stood behind their seats, drank ink, and lost their ceremonial knife.
translations.idiomatic: Men with omissions, sloppy writing, or carelessness stood behind their seats, drank ink, and lost their ceremonial knife, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後齊宴宗室禮，皇帝常服，別殿西廂東向。

translations.literal: The Later Qi rite for feasting the imperial clan: the emperor in regular dress sat in a separate hall in the western wing facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi rite for feasting the imperial clan: the emperor in regular dress sat in a separate hall in the western wing facing east, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 七廟子孫皆公服，無官者，單衣介幘，集神武門。

translations.literal: Descendants of the seven temples all wore official dress; those without office wore single garments with headband caps and assembled at the Shenwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the seven temples all wore official dress; those without office wore single garments with headband caps and assembled at the Shenwu Gate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 宗室尊卑，次於殿庭。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen by seniority lined up in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen by seniority lined up in the hall courtyard, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 七十者二人扶拜，八十者扶而不拜。

translations.literal: Those seventy were supported by two in bowing; those eighty were supported but did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Men seventy were supported by two in bowing; those eighty were supported but did not bow, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 升殿就位，皇帝興，宗室伏。

translations.literal: Ascending the hall to their places, when the emperor rose the clansmen bowed prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending the hall to their places, when the emperor rose the clansmen bowed prostrate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝坐，乃興拜而坐。

translations.literal: When the emperor seated himself they rose, bowed, and seated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor seated himself they rose, bowed, and seated themselves, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 尊者南面，卑者北面，皆以西為上。

translations.literal: The honored faced south, the lowly north; all took west as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: honored faced south, the lowly north; all took west as the place of honor, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 八十者一坐。

translations.literal: Those eighty were granted one seat.
translations.idiomatic: Men eighty were granted one seat, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 再至，進絲竹之樂。

translations.literal: At the second round, string and bamboo music was brought in.
translations.idiomatic: During the second round, string and bamboo music was brought in, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 三爵畢，宗室避席，待詔而後復位。

translations.literal: When three cups were finished the clansmen left their mats and waited for the summons before returning to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Once three cups were finished the clansmen left their mats and waited for the summons before returning to their places, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 乃行無算爵。

translations.literal: Then the uncounted cup round proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Then the uncounted cup round proceeded, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 正晦泛舟，則皇帝乘輿，鼓吹至行殿。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the first month for boating, the emperor rode the palanquin with musicians to the traveling hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the full moon of the first month for boating, the emperor rode the palanquin with musicians to the traveling hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 升禦坐，乘版輿，以與王公登舟，置酒。

translations.literal: He ascended the imperial seat, rode the platform palanquin, boarded the boat with princes and dukes, and wine was set out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the imperial seat, rode the platform palanquin, boarded the boat with princes and dukes, and wine was set out, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 非預泛者，坐於便幕。

translations.literal: Those not attending the boating sat in the side pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Men not attending the boating sat in the side pavilion, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 仲春令辰，陳養老禮。

translations.literal: In the second month on the appointed day the elder-care rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month on the appointed day the elder-care rite was performed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 先一日，三老五更齋于國學。

translations.literal: One day before, the Three Elders and Five Worthies fasted at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: One day before, the Three Elders and Five Worthies fasted at the Directorate of Education, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝進賢冠、玄紗袍，至璧雍，入總章堂。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the cap of advancing worthies and dark gauze robe, came to the Bi Yong, and entered the Zongzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: emperor wore the cap of advancing worthies and dark gauze robe, came to the Bi Yong, and entered the Zongzhang Hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 列宮懸。

translations.literal: Palace bells were arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace bells were arrayed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 王公已下及國老庶老各定位。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes and below, state elders and common elders each took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes and below, state elders and common elders each took their places, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 司徒以羽儀武賁安車，迎三老五更于國學。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education with guard of honor and armed escort in the secure carriage welcomed the Three Elders and Five Worthies from the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education with guard of honor and armed escort in the secure carriage welcomed the Three Elders and Five Worthies from the Directorate of Education, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 並進賢冠、玄服、黑舄、素帶。

translations.literal: All wore the cap of advancing worthies, dark robes, black shoes, and plain belts.
translations.idiomatic: Every wore the cap of advancing worthies, dark robes, black shoes, and plain belts, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 國子生黑介幘、青衿、單衣，乘馬從以至。

translations.literal: Directorate students in black headband caps, blue collars, and single garments rode horses following to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students in black headband caps, blue collars, and single garments rode horses following to the hall, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝釋劍，執珽，迎於門內。

translations.literal: The emperor removed his sword, took the scepter, and welcomed them inside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: emperor removed his sword, took the scepter, and welcomed them inside the gate, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 三老至門，五更去門十步，則降車以入。

translations.literal: When the Three Elders reached the gate, the Five Worthies at ten paces from the gate descended from the carriage to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Three Elders reached the gate, the Five Worthies at ten paces from the gate descended from the carriage to enter, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拜，三老五更攝齊答拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed; the Three Elders and Five Worthies adjusted their robes and returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: emperor bowed; the Three Elders and Five Worthies adjusted their robes and returned the bow, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝揖進，三老在前，五更在後，升自右階，就筵。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed and advanced; the Three Elders in front, the Five Worthies behind, ascended by the right steps and took their mats.
translations.idiomatic: emperor bowed and advanced; the Three Elders in front, the Five Worthies behind, ascended by the right steps and took their mats, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 三老坐，五更立。

translations.literal: The Three Elders sat; the Five Worthies stood.
translations.idiomatic: Three Elders sat; the Five Worthies stood, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升堂，北面。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the hall facing north.
translations.idiomatic: emperor ascended the hall facing north, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 公卿升自左階，北面。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes ascended by the left steps facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes ascended by the left steps facing north, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 三公授幾杖，卿正履，國老庶老各就位。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes presented tables and staffs; ministers corrected their shoes; state elders and common elders each took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Three Dukes presented tables and staffs; ministers corrected their shoes; state elders and common elders each took their places, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拜三老，群臣皆拜。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed to the Three Elders; all ministers bowed.
translations.idiomatic: emperor bowed to the Three Elders; all ministers bowed, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 不拜五更。

translations.literal: He did not bow to the Five Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not bow to the Five Worthies, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 乃坐，皇帝西向，肅拜五更。

translations.literal: Then he seated himself; the emperor faced west and bowed respectfully to the Five Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Then he seated himself; the emperor faced west and bowed respectfully to the Five Worthies, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 進珍羞酒食，親袒割，執醬以饋，執爵以酳。

translations.literal: Delicacies and wine were brought in; he bared his shoulder to cut, held the sauce to feed them, held the cup to rinse their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Delicacies and wine were brought in; he bared his shoulder to cut, held the sauce to feed them, held the cup to rinse their mouths, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 以次進五更。

translations.literal: In order he advanced to the Five Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In order he advanced to the Five Worthies, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又設酒酏于國老庶老。

translations.literal: Wine and fermented milk were also set out for state elders and common elders.
translations.idiomatic: Wine and fermented milk were also set out for state elders and common elders, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升禦坐，三老乃論五孝六順，典訓大綱。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the imperial seat; the Three Elders then expounded the five filialities and six harmonies — the great outline of canonical instruction.
translations.idiomatic: emperor ascended the imperial seat; the Three Elders then expounded the five filialities and six harmonies — the great outline of canonical instruction, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝虛躬請受，禮畢而還。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed empty-bodied to request instruction; when the rite was complete he returned.
translations.idiomatic: emperor bowed empty-bodied to request instruction; when the rite was complete he returned, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又都下及外州人年七十已上，賜鳩杖黃帽。

translations.literal: Also in the capital and outer provinces, those seventy and above were given dove staffs and yellow caps.
translations.idiomatic: Further, in the capital and outer provinces, those seventy and above were given dove staffs and yellow caps, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 有敕即給，不為常也。

translations.literal: When there was an edict it was given; this was not regular.
translations.idiomatic: Once there was an edict it was given; this was not regular, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 後周保定三年，陳養老之禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding of Later Zhou the elder-care rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Zhou Baoding 3 the elder-care rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 乙太傅、燕國公於謹為三老。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Duke Yuwen Jin of Yan was appointed Three Elder.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Duke Yuwen Jin of Yan was appointed Three Elder, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 有司具禮擇日，高祖幸太學以食之。

translations.literal: The relevant office prepared the rite and chose the day; Gaozu attended the Grand Academy to feast him.
translations.idiomatic: relevant office prepared the rite and chose the day; Gaozu attended the Grand Academy to feast him, as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 事見謹傳。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in Jin's biography.
translations.idiomatic: affair is recorded in Jin's biography, as prescribed.
